In the situation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]], define
$d^A(\lambda)$ for an ADDABLE $i$-node $A$ to be the number of addable
$i$-nodes strictly ABOVE $A$ minus the number of removable $i$-nodes strictly
ABOVE $A$. Define the codegree of a standard tableau $T$ by
$\operatorname{codeg}(\varnothing):=0$ and
$\operatorname{codeg}(T):=d^A(\mu^A)+\operatorname{codeg}(T_{\le d-1})$, where
$A$ is the node containing $d$ and $\mu^A=\mu\setminus A$. Define the defect of
a residue content $\alpha\in Q_+$ by
$\operatorname{def}(\alpha):=(\Lambda_0,\alpha)-(\alpha,\alpha)/2$ (the
symmetric form of [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). Then for every
partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$:

1. $d_A(\mu)+d^A(\mu^A)=d_i(\mu)+1$ where $i$ is the residue of the removable
node $A$ and
$d_i(\mu)=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes of }\mu\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes of }\mu\}$;

2. $d_i(\mu)=(\Lambda_0-\alpha,\alpha_i)$;

3. $\operatorname{def}(\alpha)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha-\alpha_i)+d_i(\mu)+1$;

4. $\deg(T)+\operatorname{codeg}(T)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha)$;

5. removing a brick does not change the codegree: if
$m\to_Tm+1\to_T\cdots\to_Td$ and $S=T_{\le m-1}$, then
$\operatorname{codeg}(S)=\operatorname{codeg}(T)$ whenever (i) $m,\dots,d$
occupy nodes in the first row of the first component of $T$, or (ii)
$d-m+1=e$ (the quantum characteristic).

No choice is used.

**Parameters.** Let $F$ be a field and $\xi\in F^\times$ with finite quantum characteristic $e=e(F,\xi)\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). We work in the NONDEGENERATE branch $\xi\ne1$; then $\xi$ is a primitive $e$-th root of unity in $F$, and all statements on this page live in one of the two sub-branches: (C0) $\operatorname{char}F=0$, or (CP) $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$ with $p\nmid e$. The Hecke parameter is written $\xi$ here; it is the letter $q$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]].

**Hecke side.** Fix the level-one fundamental weight $\Lambda_0$ of the cyclic affine type-$A$ datum with all $d_i=1$ and charge $0$ ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). With the conventions of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], $H^\Lambda_d=H_{F,\xi}(S_d)$ is the finite type-$A$ Hecke algebra $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$ ([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]), and $H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$ are its residue-content blocks ([[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]]).

**KLR side.** Use the type-$A$ specialization $Q^A$ of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] with the same $e$ and the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]: the cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$, induction appends on the right, and the grading is $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ ([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). The transported grading on $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ uses a FIXED admissible local normalising series ([[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]); a different series gives a graded-isomorphic transported algebra via $\rho'\rho^{-1}$, and the graded multiplicities studied below do not depend on the choice.

**Grading and Fock variables.** All grading shifts and all global-basis polynomials are in the variable $q$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Thus $\xi\in F^\times$ (the Hecke parameter, equal to the source's $\xi$) and $q$ (the grading variable, equal to the source's quantum variable) are INDEPENDENT data; the design's phrase "Ariki's normalization $\xi=q^2$" is retained only as the source dictionary of [Ariki 1996], whose Hecke parameters are powers of a square $q_{\rm src}^2$, and no numerical relation or specialization between $\xi$ and $q$ is imposed.

**Fock side.** Use the level-one symmetric model $\mathcal F_{\rm sym}$ of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: charge $0$, node residues $c-r$, standard vectors $M_\mu$ for ALL partitions $\mu$, basic/restricted labels the $e$-restricted partitions $RP_\alpha=\{\lambda:\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<e,\ \operatorname{cont}(\lambda)=\alpha\}$, empty component $B(\Lambda_0)$. For $\lambda\in RP$ the conjugate $\lambda'$ is $e$-regular. Write $P(\nu)$ for the independently constructed ordinary Dipper–James Specht module and $D_{\rm DJ}^{\nu}$ for its form quotient in [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]. Define $\theta(T_r)=(\xi-1)-T_r=-\xi T_r^{-1}$, the involutive sign automorphism of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. After converting right modules to left modules through the star anti-involution, the intrinsic restricted Murphy simple with label $\lambda$ is $\theta$-pullback of $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}$, not the untwisted ordinary module. This is an ungraded convention dictionary. The pullback can move blocks: on the multiplicative Jucys–Murphy elements $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$, so charge-zero residue content is sent from $\alpha$ to $-\alpha$. Thus the ordinary module before pullback has the conjugate content; no claim identifies it untwisted inside the same block. At $\xi=1$ the separate specialization theorem [[cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary]] identifies $\theta$ with sign tensoring over every field; $\xi=1$ remains outside the present nondegenerate regime.

No choice principle is used.

The type-$A$ datum and the grading are batch-24 clauses; the transport statement is the graded block isomorphism of [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]] with [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]. The Fock-side residues, the restricted labels and the empty component are batch-9/batch-23 clauses. The ordinary dictionary uses the actual universal module-and-form comparison [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]], not a rename of a cellular module. field_changes.after:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A field $F$, a parameter $\xi\in F^\times$ of finite quantum
characteristic $e\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ with $\xi\ne1$, the level-one datum
$(\Lambda_0,0)$ of the cyclic affine type-$A$ Cartan datum, the Hecke and KLR
towers with their blocks, and the symmetric level-one Fock model.

[F1] The quantum characteristic $e(F,\xi)$ and the requirement that a finite
quantum characteristic forces $\xi$ to be a primitive $e$-th root of unity in
the nondegenerate branch are as declared in
[[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]].

[F2] The level-one cyclic affine type-$A$ datum has all $d_i=1$, charge $0$,
and $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\langle\Lambda_0,h_i\rangle=\delta_{i,0}$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]).

[F3] The standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient is the quotient of the KLR
algebra by the first-strand cyclotomic ideal, with the diagrammatic grading
$\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2d_i$ and $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]],
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]).

[F4] In the symmetric level-one model the node residues are $c-r$, the
standard vectors $M_\mu$ are indexed by all partitions, the restricted labels
are the $e$-restricted partitions of the given content and the empty component
is the basic crystal $B(\Lambda_0)$
([[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]).

[F5] The sign automorphism $\theta(T_r)=(\xi-1)-T_r$ is an involution of the
finite Hecke algebra and satisfies $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$ on the multiplicative
Jucys--Murphy elements ([[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]).

[F6] The Hecke side is $H^\Lambda_d=H_{F,\xi}(S_d)$
(`prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras`),
whose residue-content blocks are the $e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$
(`def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks`); the blockwise
KLR isomorphism and the inherited transported grading are
`thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism` and
`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading`, and the ordinary
Specht-form dictionary is
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell`.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The level-one cyclotomic relation.** By [F2], $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\delta_{i,0}$, so the cyclotomic polynomial of the level-one Hecke presentation is $\prod_i(X_1-\xi^i)^{(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)}=X_1-1$ and the KLR first-strand cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i,0}}e(i)=0$ [F2, F3]. Consequently the level-one Hecke quotient is the finite type-$A$ Hecke algebra with $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$ and its residue-content blocks are the $e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$, as stated by the level-one finite-Hecke supplier [F6]. [F2, F3, F6]

1.2 **The two sub-branches.** In characteristic zero a primitive $e$-th root of unity always exists, so (C0) is nonempty for every $e$; in characteristic $p>0$ the hypothesis $p\nmid e$ makes $X^e-1$ separable with $e$ distinct roots in the algebraic closure and the roots of unity form a cyclic group, so a primitive $e$-th root exists in $F$ exactly when the given $\xi$ is one, which the finite quantum characteristic guarantees [F1]. Thus in both branches $\xi$ is a primitive $e$-th root of unity and $\xi\ne1$ as declared. [F1]

1.3 **Grading and transport conventions.** The KLR degrees are $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$ and $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ in the type-$A$ specialization with all $d_i=1$ [F3]. Transporting along the blockwise KLR isomorphism and an admissible local normalising series gives each Hecke block a $\mathbb Z$-grading, nontrivial on the corollary's level-one $e=2$ rank-two sector and trivial on a one-dimensional block, and two admissible series differ by the graded automorphism $\rho'\rho^{-1}$, so all graded multiplicities below are independent of the choice [F6]. [F3, F6]

1.4 **The Fock conventions.** The symmetric model has charge $0$, residues $c-r$, standard vectors indexed by all partitions, restricted labels the $e$-restricted partitions $RP_\alpha$, and empty component $B(\Lambda_0)$; the conjugate of a restricted partition is $e$-regular [F4]. These are exactly the labels used by the global basis expansions of the page. [F4]

1.5 **The theta dictionary and content reflection.** The sign automorphism satisfies $\theta(T_r)=(\xi-1)-T_r=-\xi T_r^{-1}$ and is an involution [F5]. On the finite level-one tower the Jucys--Murphy elements are the palindromic words $X_j=\xi^{1-j}T_{j-1}\cdots T_1T_1\cdots T_{j-1}$; applying $\theta$ to this palindrome inverts the generators in reversed order, which reproduces the same palindrome inverted, and the $2j-2$ factors contribute $(-\xi)^{2j-2}=\xi^{2j-2}$, so $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$ exactly, the scalar $1$ being the product of the displayed factors [F5]. On a generalized eigenvector with $X_jv=\xi^iv$ one therefore has $X_j^{-1}v=\xi^{-i}v$, so pulling back along the involution $\theta$ reflects every residue $i$ to $-\xi$-power $i\mapsto-i$ and hence sends charge-zero content $\alpha$ to $-\alpha$; the ordinary module carries the conjugate content before pullback and is not identified untwisted in the same block [F5, F6]. [F5, F6]

2.1 **The ungraded convention dictionary and no choice.** After converting right modules to left modules through the star anti-involution, the intrinsic restricted Murphy simple with label $\lambda$ is the $\theta$-pullback of $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}$, by the ordinary Specht-form comparison of [F6]; the Laurent-unit form factor of that comparison preserves radicals, so it includes the zero-quotient case and the dictionary is stable under applying the involution twice [F6]. The parameter $\xi$ of the Hecke algebra and the grading variable $q$ are kept independent, and no numerical relation between them is imposed. Every clause of the definition is a convention or a finite computation, so no choice principle is used. [F5, F6, given] ∎

before.statement:
Set wedge^N V_aff=V_aff^tensorN/Ker A_N, with u_(m1)∧…∧u_(mN) its images. Fix normal order m1>…>mN. The quotient is U_q-stable for the fixed coproduct. For l<m write m−l=a e+b, a≥0, 0≤b<e. The exact local relations are: u_l∧u_l=0; u_l∧u_m=−u_m∧u_l if b=0; u_l∧u_m=−q^-1 u_m∧u_l if a=0,b>0; and if a>0,b>0,
u_l∧u_m=−q^-1u_m∧u_l−u_(l+ae)∧u_(m−ae)−q^-1u_(m−ae)∧u_(l+ae).
Repeat this same recurrence on its remaining unordered pair; the gap drops by e in that branch. All correction indices are strictly between l,m, with the same sum and residue multiset. The integral lattice W_A is the image of the Laurent tensor lattice and equals the A-span of the normal basis after the next theorem. The zero chart W0 is separately its A0 normal-basis span; W_A/qW_A is0 and is not a crystal residue. The numerical energy criterion uses H_op from the explicitly OP channel; H_op>0 is equivalent to normal decreasing indices, not a claim about our tensor crystal projector.
before.strategy: Use S=−q t and Leclerc Proposition8. Its full two-factor Bernstein computation gives the displayed three cases, not a truncated sum with constant coefficients. For a>0,b>0, (l+ae,m−ae)=(m−b,l+b) is already decreasing; the third pair is its reverse and has gap ae−b=(a−1)e+(e−b), so repeated application is finite. Equal residues follow from the symmetric loop-shift action on the diagonal kernel; repeated entries vanish. All relations lie in Ker(S+1) and the kernel/gap induction gives generation. U-stability follows from the checked Hecke intertwiners. The later normalized-R bridge proves the exact braiding kernel; it does not replace this finite computation. Integral coefficients are Laurent integers, and positive/infinity crystal charts require separate rings.

after.title: The finite q-wedge space and the normal-ordering relations
after.statement:
For $N\ge1$ let $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ carry the affine Hecke action and put
$W_N:=V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}\big/\ker A_N$, where $A_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$;
write $u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}$ for the image of the pure tensor, and let
$\wedge$ denote this product. Call an index tuple **normal** (or normally
ordered) if $m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N$, and set $W_A:=\sum_{\text{normal }I}\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\,u_I$,
$W_0:=\bigoplus_{\text{normal }I}\mathbb Z[q]\,u_I$, where $u_I$ is the image of
the corresponding ordered wedge.

For $l<m$ write $m-l=ae+b$ with $a\ge0$, $0\le b<e$ (so $a=\lfloor(m-l)/e\rfloor$
and $b$ is the residue difference). The **normal-ordering relations** are:

$$u_l\wedge u_l=0;\qquad u_l\wedge u_m=-u_m\wedge u_l\quad(b=0);\qquad u_l\wedge u_m=-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l\quad(a=0,\ b>0);$$

$$u_l\wedge u_m=-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l-u_{l+ae}\wedge u_{m-ae}-q^{-1}u_{m-ae}\wedge u_{l+ae}\quad(a>0,\ b>0),$$

where the last line is to be read as a relation in $W_N$ and is applied
recursively to its two remaining unordered pairs; each recursion step strictly
decreases the gap of the unordered pair it rewrites and keeps every index
between $l$ and $m$, so the procedure terminates. The energy normal order is
the equivalent formulation through the opposite-channel energy:
$u_{m_1}\wedge u_{m_2}$ is rewritten toward decreasing indices by
$H_{\mathrm{op}}(u_{m_1}\otimes u_{m_2})>0\iff m_1>m_2$ of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]].
after.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The quotient and charts in the Definition, with the stated affine Hecke Laurent action.

[F1] The contract of [[lem-the-q-antisymmetrizer-determines-the-finite-q-wedge-kernel]] gives $\ker A_N=\sum_i\ker(S_i+1)$ and $A_NS_i=QA_N$, where $Q=q^2$; therefore each $S_i$ induces the scalar $Q$ on $W_N$. The kernel is stable under the quantum group action.

[F2] The residue operator and its exact Laurent extension are those of [[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]]: $S(fw)=s(f)S(w)+(1-Q)Y_2(f-s(f))/(Y_1-Y_2)w$.

[F3] Each $u_m=Y^{p}v_j$ with $m=j-pe$, $1\le j\le e$, and $Y$ is invertible; the opposite energy is positive exactly for decreasing indices ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]).



## Verification

**Proof technique:** calculate the actual Laurent two-factor kernel vectors and their symmetric-loop multiples, then use finite dominance followed by inversions for termination.

1.1 Symmetric Laurent multiplication preserves $\ker(S+1)$. If $g=s(g)$, [F2] gives $S(gx)=gS(x)$, since the divided difference of $g$ is zero; this applies also to negative common loop shifts $(Y_1Y_2)^r$. On a diagonal $d_j=v_j\otimes v_j$ one has $S(d_j)=-d_j$. For $j<k$, set $w=v_j\otimes v_k$ and $w'=v_k\otimes v_j$; substitution gives $S(w+q^{-1}w')=-(w+q^{-1}w')$. For $j>k$ the divided differences of $Y_1,Y_2$ give $S(Y_1w)=-qY_2w'$ and $S(Y_2w')=-qY_1w+(Q-1)Y_2w'$, so $Y_1w+q^{-1}Y_2w'$ is a $-1$ eigenvector. These calculations take place in the original Laurent tensor space. Their images vanish in every adjacent pair of slots by [F1]. [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 Diagonal and equal-residue relations. A repeated-index tensor is $(Y_1Y_2)^pd_j$ and hence vanishes. If $l<m$ have the same residue, write $l=j-(r+a)e$, $m=j-re$ with $a>0$. The symmetric multiple $(Y_1Y_2)^r(Y_1^a+Y_2^a)d_j$ is in $\ker(S+1)$ by step 1.1; its image is $u_l\wedge u_m+u_m\wedge u_l$, giving the equal-residue relation. No individual nonsymmetric loop multiplier of a kernel vector has been assumed to preserve the kernel. [step 1.1, F1, F3, algebra]

2.2 Distinct residues without wrapping. Write $l=j-pe$, $m=k-re$ with $j<k$. Then $m-l=(p-r)e+(k-j)=ae+b$, so $p=r+a$ and $b=k-j$. If $a=0$, the symmetric common shift $(Y_1Y_2)^r(w+q^{-1}w')$ gives $u_l\wedge u_m=-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l$. If $a>0$, multiply the same kernel vector by the symmetric Laurent polynomial $(Y_1Y_2)^r(Y_1^a+Y_2^a)$. The four resulting images are, with coefficients $1,q^{-1},1,q^{-1}$, respectively $(l,m)$, $(m-ae,l+ae)$, $(l+ae,m-ae)$, $(m,l)$. Their sum is zero, which is precisely the fourth displayed relation. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 Distinct residues across the representative boundary. If $j>k$, the same expressions have $p-r=a+1$ and $b=e+k-j$. The wrapped base kernel vector of step 1.1 is $h=Y_1w+q^{-1}Y_2w'$. For $a=0$, its common shift $(Y_1Y_2)^rh$ gives the third displayed relation. For $a>0$, its symmetric multiple $(Y_1Y_2)^r(Y_1^a+Y_2^a)h$ has images $(l,m)$, $(m,l)$, $(l+ae,m-ae)$ and $(m-ae,l+ae)$ with coefficients $1,q^{-1},1,q^{-1}$. Thus it gives the same fourth relation in this case also. Together with step 2.1 this exhausts all residue and Laurent-exponent configurations. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

4.1 Pair recursion and whole-word termination. In the mixed case the correction indices are $m-b$ and $l+b$, strictly between $l$ and $m$, with gap $ae-b<ae+b$; the first correction pair is already decreasing, and the reverse pair can be rewritten recursively. For a word of length $N$, fix its original interval $[L,U]$ and total sum $T$. Every branch stays among the finitely many integer tuples in $[L,U]^N$ of sum $T$. Sort a tuple decreasingly and list its first $N-1$ prefix sums. Balancing a pair of extremes strictly decreases this list in lexicographic order: the sums of the largest $r$ coordinates cannot increase, and at least one decreases since the sorted multisets differ. A leading adjacent swap preserves this list and decreases by one the number of pairs of positions whose indices are increasing. Hence the lexicographic pair consisting of prefix-sum list and inversion count strictly decreases along each nonzero branch. Its range is finite, so rewriting terminates. Equal adjacent indices vanish; a terminal nonzero word is strictly decreasing. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, given, algebra]

5.1 Charts and energy. All coefficients in the displayed relations belong to $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Step 4.1 therefore expresses every Laurent tensor-lattice image in the $A$-span of the normal wedges; conversely each normal wedge is such an image. These two lattices equal $W_A$. Its positive chart is the separately defined $\mathbb Z[q]$-span $W_0$, and $q$ is a unit on $W_A$, so $W_A/qW_A=0$. The energy criterion is exactly [F3] and concerns the opposite channel. These computations establish every displayed relation and chart assertion in the Definition, using the kernel contract in [F1]. [step 4.1, F1, F3, given, algebra] ∎

before.title: The semi-infinite q-wedge Fock space and its q-adic topology
before.statement: For charge M form the algebraic direct limit of the finite wedge spaces by appending u_(M−N),u_(M−N−1),… to a prefix of length N. Equivalently quotient the eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Normal semi-infinite words have i_k=Lambda_k−k+1+M with Lambda a partition, and the vacuum is u_M∧u_(M−1)∧…. Let F_A=⊕_Lambda A|Lambda;M>, F0=⊕ A0|Lambda;M>, F_Z0=⊕ Z[q]|Lambda;M>. The full-field separated q-adic topology is induced by q^n F0, NEVER q^nF_A=F_A. A finite A0 label component completes to a Q[[q]] lattice, and its full-field component completes to Q((q)) tensor_Q(q)F_mu. Separately the finite Z[q] chart completes to a Z[[q]] lattice; that integral completion is not identified with Q((q)) or asserted to be a Q-vector topology. Fix j(M)∈{1,…,e}, M=j−ae. The vacuum P-weight Omega_M is normalized by Omega0=Lambda0 and Omega_M−Omega_(M−1)=wt(u_M). Explicitly if M=te+r,0≤r<e, Omega_M=Lambda_r−[e t(t−1)/2+t r]delta. A partition's weight is Omega_M−Σ_cells alpha_(content+M), and its size is a separate grading. The Cartan d eigenvalue is Omega_M(d) minus the number of residue0 cells, not partition size. No false Omega_M=Omega_(M−e)+delta periodicity is asserted.
before.strategy: Append the exact ground tail. If a finite word becomes nonnormal across the cutoff, integral straightening stays inside its index interval. A tail filled with every integer in that interval eventually forces any offending term to0; ordered words stabilize to the displayed beta-number partition words. Their independence follows from sufficiently large finite normal-basis independence. Thus the algebraic quotient/direct limit has this basis and Laurent/integral/local charts. In the A0 chart every nonzero finite coordinate has finite valuation, so the topology is separated; the A0 lattice completion is Q[[q]] and localization gives the full-field Laurent-series completion Q((q)); the separate Z[q] chart completion is Z[[q]]. The vacuum weights follow by adding one affine vector u_M; summing its loop power a(M)=(j−M)/e gives the explicit quadratic delta shift. This discharges charge rather than silently changing the full d-action. In charge0 Omega0=Lambda0 and residues remain c−r.

after.title: The semi-infinite q-wedge Fock space and its q-adic topology
after.statement:
Fix a **charge** $M\in\mathbb Z$ and let $W_N$ be the finite q-wedge spaces of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]. For $r\le s$ define
the connecting map
$\varphi_{r,s}(u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r})
=u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r}\wedge u_{M-r}\wedge u_{M-r-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-s+1}$,
so that new entries are the consecutive ground tail
$u_{M-N},u_{M-N-1},\dots$ appended to a prefix of length $N$. The **charge-$M$
Fock space** is the algebraic direct limit $F^{(M)}:=\varinjlim_{N}W_N$ of the
finite wedge spaces along these maps; equivalently it is the quotient of the
eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Write
$|\lambda;M\rangle$ for the image of the normally ordered semi-infinite word
with entries $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ indexed by the positive parts of the
partition $\lambda$, so that the vacuum $\varnothing$ corresponds to
$u_M\wedge u_{M-1}\wedge u_{M-2}\wedge\cdots$.

The **Laurent, positive and integral charts** of $F^{(M)}$ are

$$F_A:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_0:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A_0\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_{\mathbb Z0}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Z[q]\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}],\ A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}.$$

The **separated q-adic topology** on the full field space is the one induced by
the filtration $q^nF_0$, never by $q^nF_A=F_A$; a finite $A_0$-label component
completes to a $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$-lattice, and the full-field component completes
to $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}F^{(M)}_\mu$ for the label-weight
pieces. Separately, the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart completes to a
$\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$-lattice; this completion is not identified with
$\mathbb Q((q))$ and is not asserted to carry a $\mathbb Q$-vector-space
topology.

**Vacuum weights.** For $M=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$
the vacuum $P$-weight $\Omega_M$ is normalised by $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$ and
$\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$; explicitly, if $M=te+r$ with
$0\le r<e$, then

$$\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-\Bigl(\frac{e\,t(t-1)}{2}+tr\Bigr)\delta.$$

The weight of the partition $\lambda$ is
$\Omega_M-\sum_{\text{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$, its size $|\lambda|$ is a separate
grading, and the $d$-eigenvalue is $\Omega_M(d)$ minus the number of residue-$0$
cells; no periodicity $\Omega_M=\Omega_{M-e}+\delta$ is asserted.
after.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The charge $M$, the finite wedge spaces $W_N$, the connecting maps $\varphi_{r,s}$, the direct limit $F^{(M)}$, the three charts, the filtration $q^nF_0$, and the normalisation of $\Omega_M$.

[F1] The normally ordered wedges with strictly decreasing indices are a field basis and a Laurent basis in every $W_N$, and the straightening stays inside the index interval ([[thm-normally-ordered-q-wedges-form-a-basis]]).

[F2] $Y_ju_m=u_{m-e}$ inside the $j$-th slot is the loop operator; the residue of $u_m$ is $m\bmod e$ and $\mathrm{wt}(u_m)=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}+a\delta$ for $m=j-ae$ ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]).

[F3] The loop operator $Y=z$ itself shifts a slot by $-e$, so its $e$-th power shifts it by $-e^2$; simultaneous translations preserve local index differences and hence the finite wedge relations. The levels of the vector-weight differences and $\delta$ are $0$ ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]], [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]).



## Verification

**Proof technique:** show the semi-infinite words stabilise and agree with the partition indexing, then compute the vacuum weights by summing the loop exponents.

1.1 Finite-stage spanning and ordered-tail stabilization. Start with a finite word of length $r$ and choose $S\ge r$ so that the last appended ground index $L=M-S+1$ is below all its original indices. Its image at stage $S$ has $S$ entries, all at least $L$. By [F1], its finite straightening is a finite sum of normal tuples $n_1>\cdots>n_S\ge L$. For each resulting tuple put $\lambda_j=n_j-(M-j+1)$. Then $\lambda_S\ge0$ and $\lambda_j\ge\lambda_{j+1}$, so extending by zeros gives a partition. Every subsequent connecting map appends ground indices $M-S,M-S-1,\ldots$, strictly below the normal tuple's last entry; that image is already normal and is the longer prefix of the same partition word. Thus every direct-limit element is a finite combination of partition words with a stable representative under these ordered-tail extensions. Maps with different finite codomains are not equated. [F1, given, algebra]

1.2 Direct verification of the vacuum weights. Let $M=te+r$ with $t\in\mathbb Z$ and $0\le r<e$, and put $\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-[et(t-1)/2+tr]\delta$. It gives $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$. If $r>0$, subtraction of the formula for $M-1=te+(r-1)$ gives $\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\Lambda_r-\Lambda_{r-1}-t\delta=\lambda_r-t\delta$. Here $u_M=z^{-t}v_r$, so this is exactly $\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$ by [F2]. If $r=0$, use $M-1=(t-1)e+(e-1)$: subtraction gives $\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\Lambda_0-\Lambda_{e-1}+(1-t)\delta=\lambda_e+(1-t)\delta$, and $u_M=z^{1-t}v_e$ has precisely this weight. These integer identities also hold for negative $t$. The base value and this recurrence uniquely determine the weights for all integer charges. The partition label is consequently the stipulated $\Omega_M-\sum_{\mathrm{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$, whose $d$-evaluation is $\Omega_M(d)-m_0$ by the explicit datum; size remains the separate grading. No fractional change of an integer loop exponent or infinite unregularized weight sum is used. [F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 Partition indexing and direct-limit independence. An eventually-ground normal word has $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ with $\lambda_k$ weakly decreasing and eventually zero; hence the $\lambda_k$ are nonnegative and form a partition, and every partition gives such a word. For finitely many distinct partitions choose a common prefix length $N$ containing all their nonzero rows and every position where two words differ. Each partition prefix is normal and has last index $i_N\ge M-N+1$. Its next appended index is $M-N$, strictly smaller, so every later image remains a normal basis word, and the distinct partition images remain distinct. If a finite linear combination vanished in the algebraic direct limit, it would vanish at some common later finite stage: a colimit relation uses finitely many connecting-map relations, which can all be moved to that common stage. Independence of the finite normal basis in [F1] then forces every coefficient to vanish. Together with step 1.1, this proves the partition basis without assuming that arbitrary finite words survive tail attachment. [step 1.1, F1, given, algebra]

3.1 The charts and the topology. Each displayed chart is free on the partition basis over its own ring. Both $F_A$ and $F_0$ contain $F_{\mathbb Z0}$, and $F_A\cap F_0=F_{\mathbb Z0}$ coefficientwise: an integral Laurent polynomial is regular at zero exactly when it has no negative powers. Neither chart is identified with the other. A nonzero vector of the local $A_0$-chart has finitely many nonzero coefficients, each of finite $q$-valuation, so $\bigcap_{n\ge0}q^nF_0=0$. On each finite label component the completion of $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ is $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$, and inverting $q$ gives the field completion $\mathbb Q((q))$; the corresponding full-field component is $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}F^{(M)}_\mu$. Separately the completion of the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart is $\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$. The Laurent lattice has $qF_A=F_A$ and therefore supplies no separated $q$-adic filtration. These statements concern the componentwise completions stipulated in the Definition; no full infinite direct sum is identified with a finite-rank completed lattice. [step 2.1, given, algebra]

4.1 Conclusion. The charge-$M$ Fock space is the algebraic direct limit of the finite wedge spaces along the ground tails, with a basis indexed by all partitions, the three charts $F_A,F_0,F_{\mathbb Z0}$ are distinct free lattices, the separated topology is induced by $q^nF_0$ (never by $q^nF_A$), and the vacuum weights are $\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-(\frac{et(t-1)}2+tr)\delta$ for $M=te+r$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 1.2] ∎

before.statement: Over Q(q) put Q=q², c=Q−1. Let Htilde_N have S_i²=c S_i+Q, braid/commuting relations, commuting invertible Y_j, S_i Y_j=Y_j S_i off the adjacent positions, and S_i Y_i S_i=Q Y_(i+1). Y_j multiplies the jth loop z, so u_(j−ae)=Y^a v_j; it is NOT z^-1. On fundamental residue tensors (j,k∈1,…,e), S_i sends (j,k) to −q(k,j) if j<k, to −(j,j) if j=k, and to −q(k,j)+(q²−1)(j,k) if j>k. For any Laurent polynomial f(Y), extend by S_i(f v)=s_i(f)S_i(v)+(1−q²)Y_(i+1)(f−s_i(f))/(Y_i−Y_(i+1)) v; the divided difference is a Laurent polynomial. This defines the action on all affine vectors. Equivalently the Leclerc generator t_i=−q^-1 S_i has roots q^-1,−q. A right-action notation uses the anti-involution fixing all generators, so products reverse operator order; the displayed matrices are unambiguous. The action commutes with the fixed U_q action (including total d). Put S_w by reduced words and A_N=Σ_(w∈S_N)S_w.

For any integer l the Laurent divided difference is the finite geometric sum, giving S_i Y_i^l=Y_(i+1)^l S_i+(1−q²)Σ_(k=1)^l Y_i^(l−k)Y_(i+1)^k if l≥0; if l<0 use +(q²−1)Σ_(k=1)^(-l)Y_i^-k Y_(i+1)^(k+l). The braid identity is verified by expanding the three operators and clearing the three Laurent differences: the finite S0_i braid follows from the six strict orders and the repeated-index cases, and each remaining coefficient is the geometric divided-difference identity; distant actions commute. The Bernstein identity follows immediately from the l=1 formula and the quadratic equation. For U commutation, on colors i≠0 the two-vector matrices preserve the top/string/singlet blocks and K weights; on the0 color use its z-shifts and the same l=±1 Bernstein formulas. Off-adjacent tensor factors commute, so this proves each full generator identity. Total d commutes because each summand preserves total loop degree. after.title: The affine Hecke algebra and its commuting action on tensor powers of the vector representation
after.statement:
Fix $e\ge2$ and keep all conventions of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]:
the Cartan datum, the space $V_{\mathrm{aff}}=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q(q)u_m$
with $u_m=z^av_j$ ($m=j-ae$, $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$), the operators
$K_h,E_i,F_i$, the classical weights $\lambda_j=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}$, and the
fixed coproduct $\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h$,
$\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$,
$\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ of
[[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]].
Put $Q:=q^2$ and $c:=Q-1$, and let $Y_j$ denote the operator "multiply the $j$-th
tensor factor by $z$", so that $Y_j$ is invertible with
$Y_ju_m=u_{m-e}$ in the $j$-th slot and different $Y_j$ commute.

**The affine Hecke algebra $\tilde H_N$.** For $N\ge1$, $\tilde H_N$ is the
unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra with generators $S_1,\dots,S_{N-1}$ and invertible
$Y_1^{\pm1},\dots,Y_N^{\pm1}$ subject to

$$S_i^2=(Q-1)S_i+Q,\qquad S_iS_{i+1}S_i=S_{i+1}S_iS_{i+1},\qquad S_iS_j=S_jS_i\quad(|i-j|\ge2),$$

$$Y_iY_j=Y_jY_i,\qquad S_iY_j=Y_jS_i\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad S_iY_iS_i=QY_{i+1}.$$

The element $t_i:=-q^{-1}S_i$ then satisfies $(t_i-q^{-1})(t_i+q)=0$; for a
reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}\in S_N$ put $S_w:=S_{i_1}\cdots S_{i_k}$
and $A_N:=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$ (well defined by the braid relations).

**The two-vector operator and its extension.** On residue tensors
$v_j\otimes v_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$) set

$$S(v_j\otimes v_k)=\begin{cases}-q\,v_k\otimes v_j,&j<k,\\ -\,v_j\otimes v_j,&j=k,\\ -q\,v_k\otimes v_j+(Q-1)v_j\otimes v_k,&j>k.\end{cases}$$

For a Laurent monomial $f=Y_1^pY_2^q$ define, with $s(f):=Y_2^pY_1^q$ the
swap of the two loop variables,

$$S(f\,w):=s(f)\,S(w)+(1-Q)\,Y_2\,\frac{f-s(f)}{Y_1-Y_2}\,w\qquad(w\in V\otimes V),$$

and extend linearly; the quotient $(f-s(f))/(Y_1-Y_2)$ is a Laurent polynomial,
so $S$ is a well-defined linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$.
On $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ the generator $S_i$ acts by this operator on
the tensor factors $i,i+1$ and $Y_j$ acts on the $j$-th factor as above; this
defines the **affine Hecke action**. The whole action commutes with the derived quantum group $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$ (the generators $E_i,F_i$ and $K_h$ with $h$ in the span of the simple coroots). Each $S_i$, and therefore $A_N$, also preserves total loop degree and commutes with the full affine quantum-group action. The individual loops instead satisfy $K_dY_jK_d^{-1}=qY_j$. Products are composed as left operators; right-action notation reverses their order using the anti-involution fixing the generators.
after.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Laurent tensor space and its vector action from [[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]], the displayed operators $S_i,Y_j$, and the fixed coproduct from [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]].

[F1] The vector basis has $u_m=z^av_j$ with $m=j-ae$, $E_i u_m=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}u_{m-1}$, $F_i u_m=\delta_{m\equiv i}u_{m+1}$, and $K_i v_j=q^{\delta_{i,j}-\delta_{i,j-1}}v_j$. In particular $E_0=zE_0^{\mathrm{fin}}$, $F_0=z^{-1}F_0^{\mathrm{fin}}$, $K_du_m=q^a u_m$, and $\mathrm{wt}(u_{m-e})=\mathrm{wt}(u_m)+\delta$ ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]).

[F2] The coproduct is $\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h$, $\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, $\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$, and is coassociative ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** establish the finite residue identities and the divided-difference identities, combine them for the full Laurent Hecke action, and verify coproduct commutation in an ordered residue window for each color.

1.1 Write $x=Y_1,y=Y_2$, let $s$ swap them, and set $D(f)=y(f-s(f))/(x-y)$. For an integer $l>0$, $(x^l-y^l)/(x-y)=\sum_{r=0}^{l-1}x^{l-1-r}y^r$; for $l<0$ it is $-\sum_{r=1}^{-l}x^{-r}y^{r+l-1}$, obtained by factoring $x^{-l}y^{-l}$ from the positive formula, and for $l=0$ it is zero. Factoring a common Laurent monomial proves that $D$ preserves the Laurent ring. The identity $D(fg)=D(f)g+s(f)D(g)$ follows by subtracting $s(f)s(g)$ from $fg$. With $d=y/(x-y)$, $s(d)=-x/(x-y)$ and $d+s(d)=-1$, expansion of $D=d(1-s)$ gives $D^2=-D$ and $sD+Ds=1-s$. These rational computations are identities on Laurent polynomials because the finite sums show that all the operators preserve that ring. [given, algebra]

1.2 Let $T$ be the displayed residue matrix. For $a=v_j\otimes v_k$, $b=v_k\otimes v_j$, $j<k$, one has $T^2a=Qa-qc b$ and $T^2b=-qc a+(Q+c^2)b$, while $T^2d_j=d_j$ on $d_j=v_j\otimes v_j$. Hence $T^2=cT+Q$. The finite braid is also an exact finite residue identity: abbreviate a triple by its order pattern $ijk$, where $1<2<3$, and let $L=T_1T_2T_1$, $R=T_2T_1T_2$. Applying the three-case matrix gives the following common values: $L(111)=R(111)=-111$; $L(112)=R(112)=-Q211$; $L(121)=R(121)=-Q121+qc211$; $L(211)=R(211)=-Q112+qc121+c211$; $L(122)=R(122)=-Q221$; $L(212)=R(212)=-Q212+qc221$; $L(221)=R(221)=-Q122+qc212+c221$; $L(123)=R(123)=-q^3 321$; $L(132)=R(132)=-q^3 231+Qc321$; $L(213)=R(213)=-q^3 312+Qc321$; $L(231)=R(231)=-q^3 132+Qc(312+231)-qc^2 321$; $L(312)=R(312)=-q^3 213+Qc(312+231)-qc^2 321$; $L(321)=R(321)=-q^3 123+Qc(213+132)-qc^2(312+231)+(c^3+Qc)321$. These thirteen patterns exhaust all triples of residues, including repeated residues for $e=2$, proving the finite braid for every $e$. [given, algebra]

1.3 For a nonzero color $i$, let $A=v_i$ be its top vector and $B=v_{i+1}$ its bottom; $K_i$ has eigenvalues $q,q^{-1}$ there and $1$ on every other residue $O$. On the four pairs $AA,AB,BA,BB$, the coproduct maps are $\Delta(E_i):(0,AA,q^{-1}AA,qAB+BA)$ and $\Delta(F_i):(BA+qAB,BB,q^{-1}BB,0)$ respectively. Applying $T$ before or after them gives respectively $T\Delta(E_i)=\Delta(E_i)T:(0,-AA,-q^{-1}AA,-qAB-BA)$ and $T\Delta(F_i)=\Delta(F_i)T:(-BA-qAB,-BB,-q^{-1}BB,0)$. For spectator pairs, $BO\mapsto AO$, $OB\mapsto OA$ under $E_i$, and $AO\mapsto BO$, $OA\mapsto OB$ under $F_i$, with other pairs killed. Since $A,B$ are consecutive residues, every spectator is below both or above both, so the order comparison and the coefficients in $T$ are unchanged by these maps. This proves residue commutation in every case. $T$ also preserves each total derived toral weight because it only permutes residues. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 On the Laurent tensor space the operator is $S=T s-cD$, with $T$ acting only on residues. It commutes with $s,D$ on coefficients. Thus $S^2=T^2-cT(sD+Ds)+c^2D^2=cT+Q-cT(1-s)-c^2D=cS+Q$ by steps 1.1 and 1.2. This proves the quadratic relation on all loop powers, rather than only on residue tensors. Off-adjacent operators commute because their residue matrices and divided differences involve disjoint positions. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 For $i\ne0$, $\Delta(E_i),\Delta(F_i)$ and the derived torals act by constant residue matrices and commute with scalar Laurent multiplication and the coefficient operators $s,D$. Together with step 1.3 and $S=T s-cD$ this proves their commutation with $S$ on every Laurent tensor. In particular the correct extension of a commutator is $[S,\Delta(X)](fw)=s(f)[S,\Delta(X)]w$, since the divided-difference terms cancel; it is not a formula with $f$ instead of $s(f)$. More generally step 1.1 gives $S(fh)=s(f)S(h)-cD(f)h$ for every Laurent tensor $h$, by applying the Leibniz identity to its residue coefficients. [step 1.1, step 1.3, F1, F2, algebra]

3.1 For three adjacent loop variables $z_1,z_2,z_3$ put $b_{ij}=-c z_j/(z_i-z_j)$, $a=b_{12}$, $b=b_{23}$, and $h=b_{13}$. Then $b_{ij}+b_{ji}=c$ and $\delta_0:=ab-h(a+b-c)=0$, the latter following on multiplying by $(z_1-z_2)(z_2-z_3)(z_1-z_3)$. Write $S_i=(T_i-b_{i,i+1})s_i+b_{i,i+1}$. Expand $S_1S_2S_1-S_2S_1S_2$ with every coefficient on the left, using $s_i b_{jk}=b_{s_i(j),s_i(k)}s_i$. After using $T_i^2=cT_i+Q$ and $T_1T_2T_1=T_2T_1T_2$, the coefficients at $1,s_1,s_2,s_1s_2,s_2s_1,s_1s_2s_1$ are respectively $(a-b)\delta_0$, $(T_1-a)\delta_0$, $-(T_2-b)\delta_0$, $0$, $0$, and $-(T_1-T_2)\delta_0$. For example the coefficient at $1$ is $a^2b+h(Q+a(c-a))-b^2a-h(Q+b(c-b))=(a-b)\delta_0$; the longest coefficient is $(T_1-a)(T_2-h)(T_1-b)-(T_2-b)(T_1-h)(T_2-a)=-(T_1-T_2)\delta_0$. Hence all coefficients vanish. Clearing the three differences gives the identity in the original Laurent tensor space, whose injection into its rational coefficient space is faithful; the operators already preserve the Laurent space by step 1.1. This proves the full braid, with no finite-loop truncation assumption. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The loop multiplication operators are invertible and commute. From step 1.1 and the extension formula, for $l>0$ one has $Sx^l=y^lS-c\sum_{r=1}^l x^{l-r}y^r$; for $l<0$ one has $Sx^l=y^lS+c\sum_{r=1}^{-l}x^{-r}y^{r+l}$, and for $l=0$ there is no correction. These identities hold on every tensor by the divided-difference Leibniz formula. In particular $Sx=yS-cy$ and $Sy=xS+cy$. Therefore $SxS=yS^2-cyS=Qy$ by step 2.1. These are precisely the Bernstein and off-adjacent loop relations in the Definition. Finally $t=-q^{-1}S$ satisfies $(t-q^{-1})(t+q)=q^{-2}(S+1)(S-Q)=0$, and equivalently $t^2=(q^{-1}-q)t+1$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 For the affine color use the ordered Laurent basis $w_1=zv_e=u_0$, $w_2=v_1=u_1$, through $w_e=v_{e-1}=u_{e-1}$. For $1\le j<e$, the extension formula gives $S(x(v_e\otimes v_j))=-q y(v_j\otimes v_e)$ and $S(y(v_j\otimes v_e))=-q x(v_e\otimes v_j)+cy(v_j\otimes v_e)$; also $S(xy(v_e\otimes v_e))=-xy(v_e\otimes v_e)$. On the other pairs the residue formula is unchanged. Thus $S$ on $w_a\otimes w_b$ is exactly the same three-case matrix in the order $w_1<\cdots<w_e$, and its extension remains the formula in step 2.2. On this basis $E_0 w_2=w_1$, $F_0w_1=w_2$, with all other images zero, because $E_0=zE_0^{\mathrm{fin}}$ and $F_0=z^{-1}F_0^{\mathrm{fin}}$. Their toral eigenvalues are $q,q^{-1}$ on $w_1,w_2$ and $1$ on spectators. Consequently precisely the finite commutation calculation of step 1.3 applies to color $0$, followed by the constant-matrix Laurent argument of step 2.2. This proves all affine-color commutators on arbitrary positive and negative loop powers. [step 1.1, step 4.1, step 1.3, step 2.2, F1, F2, algebra]

6.1 On two factors $S$ preserves total residue weight and total loop degree: $s$ swaps loop powers and $D$ has total degree zero, since its numerator is multiplied by $y$ and divided by $x-y$. Hence it commutes with $K_h\otimes K_h$ for every full toral $K_h$, including $K_d$. Each $Y_j$ commutes with $E_i,F_i$ and derived torals by [F1], but increases total loop degree by one, giving $K_dY_jK_d^{-1}=qY_j$. For $N>2$, the iterated coproduct of $E_i$ is the sum of terms $1^{\otimes(r-1)}\otimes E_i\otimes (K_i^{-1})^{\otimes(N-r)}$, and that of $F_i$ is the sum $K_i^{\otimes(r-1)}\otimes F_i\otimes1^{\otimes(N-r)}$. The two terms in the adjacent slots combine into their two-factor coproduct; a term outside those slots has either $K_i^{\pm1}\otimes K_i^{\pm1}$ or $1\otimes1$ there. Steps 2.2 and 5.1 and the toral commutation therefore prove $[S_j,\Delta^{(N)}(X)]=0$ for every full generator $X$. Individual $Y_j$ commute with the derived action for the same slotwise reason. [step 1.1, step 2.2, step 5.1, F1, F2, algebra]

7.1 The quadratic, braid, distant, loop and Bernstein identities prove the displayed affine Hecke action on the entire Laurent tensor space. The finite Hecke operators $S_i$ commute with the full quantum-group action; their products $S_w$ are well defined by reduced words and their sum $A_N$ has the same commutation and total-degree properties. The entire affine Hecke action, including each individual loop, commutes with the derived action, with the degree covariance of step 6.1. This establishes exactly the scope and normalization claimed in the Definition. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 2.2, step 5.1, step 6.1] ∎

## Remarks

The loops have degree one, whereas $S_i$ and $A_N$ have degree zero. The action
uses the fixed coproduct throughout; flipping to the opposite channel is a
separate convention change. At $q=1$, $S_i$ is the negative flip, including its
Laurent coefficients.

before.title: The level-one vector representation, its affinization and the energy function
before.statement: Use j=1,…,e as representatives (j=e represents0). The derived affine vector module V=⊕ Q(q)v_j has K_i v_j=q^(delta_(j≡i)−delta_(j≡i+1))v_j, E_i v_j=delta_(j≡i+1)v_(j−1), F_i v_j=delta_(j≡i)v_(j+1), indices cyclic. Its P_cl weight is Lambda_j−Lambda_(j−1), level0; its finite crystal has f_i b_i=b_(i+1), e_i b_(i+1)=b_i, epsilon(b_j)=Lambda_(j−1)^cl and phi(b_j)=Lambda_j^cl, level1. The full affinization has u_(j−ae)=z^a v_j of P-weight Lambda_j−Lambda_(j−1)+a delta and K_d eigen q^a. Equivalently E_i(z^a v_j)=delta_(j≡i+1) z^(a+delta_(i,0))v_(j−1), F_i(z^a v_j)=delta_(j≡i) z^(a−delta_(i,0))v_(j+1). Thus E_i u_m=delta_(m≡i+1)u_(m−1), F_i u_m=delta_(m≡i)u_(m+1). Ordinary order is u_m>u_n iff m>n. The energy is explicitly in the OPPOSITE tensor-crystal channel of KMPY bar-Delta-plus (opposite our fixed Delta): H_op(z^a b_j⊗z^b b_k)=chi(j>k)+b−a, and l(z^a b_j)=ae−j. It has the two loop-shift axioms, is constant on that channel's components, is0 on extremal diagonals and H_op>0 iff m1>m2. For a fixed charge M the ground sequence is b°_s=u_(M−s), s≥0: epsilon(b°_s)=phi(b°_(s+1)) and H_op(b°_s,b°_(s+1))=1. It is determined after the initial phase/loop vector (hence charge) is fixed, not independently of an overall loop shift. All statements include e=2.
before.strategy: Check E/F/K on the explicit u_m: each color acts on disjoint pairs (u_(i+ke),u_(i+ke+1)), with K eigen q,q^-1 and zero second powers. Different-color mixed commutators and the cycle Serre sums follow directly from these shifts; the e=2 cubic sums vanish because each squared single-color operator is0. The z-shifts on the0 edge give [d,E0]=E0,[d,F0]=−F0 and the displayed P-weights; forgetting d leaves only P_cl, not a full P-grading on finite V. Compute epsilon/phi from the arrows. KMPY uses b_j^src→b_(j+1) here and its ground indexk→u_(1−k); its MAIN bar-Delta-plus and tensor rule(2.2.13) were visually read. In that OP channel inspect the two-index rule: non-wrap moves do not change chi except at the coincident/adjacent case where the rule selects the other factor, and wrap moves change chi by the opposite of the loop-power change. This proves H_op constancy including the ties/e=2. For m1=j−ae,m2=k−be, the cases b−a positive/zero/negative prove H_op>0 iff m1>m2. The ground identities are the wrap/nonwrap calculation with adjacent integer indices. The bridge lemma later constructs the actual normalized R; no field R property is imported from the unavailable KMN source.

after.title: The level-one vector representation, its affinization and the energy function
after.statement:
Fix $e\ge2$ and let $(I,A,D,P,P^\vee,\alpha_i,h_i,\delta,d,c,q)$ be the cyclic
affine type $A$ Cartan datum of
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]], so $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ and
$q_i=q$ for all $i$. Choose once and for all the representatives
$j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ of the residues of $I$, so that $j=e$ represents the residue
$0$; all indices $j-1$, $j+1$ below are read in this representative range.

**The derived vector module.** Put $P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}:=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z h_i$, and let $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$ denote the subalgebra of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ generated by $E_i,F_i,K_h$ with $h\in P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}$. Let $V:=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{e}\mathbb Q(q)v_j$ and
define $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}$), $E_i$, $F_i$
($i\in I$) on $V$ by

$$K_hv_j:=q^{\langle\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1},h\rangle}v_j,\qquad E_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}\,v_{j-1},\qquad F_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i}\,v_{j+1},$$

where $v_0:=v_e$ and $v_{e+1}:=v_1$ are read cyclically, and $\equiv$ refers to
the residues of $I$. The vector $v_j$ has **classical weight**
$\lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}\in P_{\mathrm{cl}}$, where $\lambda_j:=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}\in P$ is the fixed representative used in the affinization, and **residue** $j\in I$. These operators give the derived $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-action; no degree operator $K_d$ is part of this finite action.

**Affinization.** The **affinization** $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis $\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$, identified
with $V\otimes\mathbb Q[z,z^{-1}]$ by $u_m:=z^av_j$ whenever
$m=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$; this representation of
$m$ is unique. On this space the full affine operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee$), $E_i,F_i$ are

$$K_hu_m:=q^{\langle\lambda_j+a\delta,h\rangle}u_m,\qquad E_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}\,u_{m-1},\qquad F_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i}\,u_{m+1},$$

so that in the $z$-picture
$E_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}z^{a+\delta_{i0}}v_{j-1}$ and
$F_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i}z^{a-\delta_{i0}}v_{j+1}$. We write
$\mathrm{wt}(u_m):=\lambda_j+a\delta\in P$ and $l(u_m):=ae-j=-m$; the
**ordinary order** is $u_m>u_n\iff m>n$.

**Crystal data.** Put $B:=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$, $B_{\mathrm{aff}}:=\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$,
and define partial operators $f_i,e_i$ on $B_{\mathrm{aff}}$ by
$f_iu_m:=u_{m+1}$ if $m\equiv i$ and $f_iu_m:=0$ otherwise, and
$e_iu_m:=u_{m-1}$ if $m\equiv i+1$ and $e_iu_m:=0$ otherwise. Let

$$\varepsilon_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i+1},\qquad \varphi_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i},\qquad \varepsilon(u_m):=\sum_i\varepsilon_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},\qquad \varphi(u_m):=\sum_i\varphi_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},$$

in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$. On the finite set $B$ the same formulas apply through
$b_j\leftrightarrow v_j$, so that $f_ib_j=b_{j+1}$ if $j\equiv i$ and $0$
otherwise, and $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ if $j\equiv i+1$ and $0$ otherwise.

**The opposite channel and its energy.** On $B_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{aff}}$
use the tensor rule $\otimes_+$

$$f_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}f_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)\ge\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes f_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)<\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}\qquad e_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}e_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)>\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes e_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)\le\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}$$

and the **energy function**

$$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k):=\chi(j>k)+b-a,\qquad \chi(j>k):=\begin{cases}1,&j>k,\\0,&j\le k,\end{cases}$$

for $a,b\in\mathbb Z$ and $j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$. For a fixed **charge**
$M\in\mathbb Z$ the **ground sequence** is $b^\circ_s:=u_{M-s}$ ($s\ge0$).
after.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The cyclic affine type $A$ Cartan datum of [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]] with residues $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$, $e\ge2$; the representatives $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$; the spaces $V$ and $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ with the displayed operators, crystal data, tensor rule and energy function; a charge $M\in\mathbb Z$ with ground sequence $b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$.

[F1] $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is presented by generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$ ($i\in I$, $h\in P^\vee$) with $K_0=1$, $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$, $K_hE_iK_h^{-1}=q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i$, $K_hF_iK_h^{-1}=q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i$, $E_iF_j-F_jE_i=\delta_{ij}(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$ and the two quantum Serre sums, $q_i=q$; any assignment satisfying these relations extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]).

[F2] The datum has $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$, $\langle\alpha_i,d\rangle=\delta_{i0}$, $\langle\Lambda_j,h_i\rangle=\delta_{ij}$, $\langle\delta,h_i\rangle=0$, $\langle\Lambda_j,d\rangle=0$ and $\langle\delta,d\rangle=1$ ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]).

[F3] For $e\ge3$, $\alpha_i=-\Lambda_{i-1}+2\Lambda_i-\Lambda_{i+1}+\delta_{i0}\delta$ and for $e=2$, $\alpha_0=2\Lambda_0-2\Lambda_1+\delta$, $\alpha_1=-2\Lambda_0+2\Lambda_1$; in all cases $\lambda_{j-1}-\lambda_j=\alpha_{j-1}$ for $2\le j\le e$, and $\lambda_e+\delta-\lambda_1=\alpha_0$ with $\lambda_j:=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}$ ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]).

[F4] The level of $\lambda\in P$ is $\langle c,\lambda\rangle$; $\lambda_j$ has level $0$ and $\Lambda_i$, as an element of $P_{\mathrm{cl}}=P/\mathbb Z\delta$, has level $1$; $q\neq q^{-1}$ in $\mathbb Q(q)$, and $q^m\ne1$ for $m\ne0$ ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]], [[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

[F5] Writing $j(m)\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ for the representative of $m\bmod e$ and $a(m):=(j(m)-m)/e$, every $m\in\mathbb Z$ has the unique expression $m=j(m)-a(m)e$; hence $u_m=z^{a(m)}v_{j(m)}$ and the assignment $m\mapsto(j(m),a(m))$ is a bijection $\mathbb Z\to\{1,\dots,e\}\times\mathbb Z$.

[F6] For all $m\in\mathbb Z$ the identities $\langle\lambda_{j(m)},h_i\rangle=\delta_{i,j(m)}-\delta_{i,j(m)-1}$ and $\langle\lambda_{j(m)}+a(m)\delta,d\rangle=a(m)$ hold ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** check the defining relations of the quantized affine algebra on the explicit cyclic shifts, compute the weights and crystal data, then verify the energy axioms on the opposite channel by a two-factor case analysis.

1.1 The derived operators on $V$ are well defined and give a $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear action of the generators. Each $E_i,F_i$ formula assigns to each $v_j$ either $0$ or a unique basis vector, and each $K_h$ multiplies $v_j$ by the nonzero scalar $q^{\langle\lambda_j,h\rangle}$, so $E_i,F_i,K_h$ are well-defined linear endomorphisms of the finite-dimensional space $V$; $K_0=\mathrm{id}$ and $K_{h+h'}=K_hK_{h'}$ hold because $\langle\lambda_j,\cdot\rangle$ is additive, so the toral assignment is a homomorphism $P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

1.2 The derived defining relations hold on $V$. For $h\in P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $j\equiv i+1$, conjugation gives $K_hE_iK_h^{-1}v_j=q^{\langle\lambda_{j-1}-\lambda_j,h\rangle}v_{j-1}$ with cyclic representatives; the weight difference is $\alpha_i$ for $j\ge2$ and $\alpha_0-\delta$ for $j=1$, and $\langle\delta,h\rangle=0$, so the coefficient is $q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}$ in both cases. Reversing the arrow gives $K_hF_iK_h^{-1}=q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i$. For distinct colors $i,t$, $E_iF_tv_j$ can be nonzero only if $j\equiv t$ and $j+1\equiv i+1$, which forces $t=i$; $F_tE_iv_j$ can be nonzero only if $j\equiv i+1$ and $j-1\equiv t$, again forcing $t=i$, so both vanish when $t\ne i$. For equal colors, $E_iF_iv_j=\delta_{j\equiv i}v_j$ and $F_iE_iv_j=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}v_j$, and $K_iv_j=q^{\delta_{i,j}-\delta_{i,j-1}}v_j$; thus $(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$ acts by $1,-1,0$ respectively when $j\equiv i$, $j\equiv i+1$, or neither. Finally $E_i^2=F_i^2=0$ because two successive steps of one color would require $i\equiv i+1$. For $e\ge3$ and $a_{it}=0$, $E_iE_t$ requires $t=i+1$ and $E_tE_i$ requires $t=i-1$, both excluded by nonadjacency; the corresponding $F$ paths require $t=i-1$ or $t=i+1$ and also vanish. For $a_{it}=-1$, the outside terms of $E_i^2E_t-(q+q^{-1})E_iE_tE_i+E_tE_i^2$ vanish by $E_i^2=0$; its middle path would require, from right to left, residues $i+1\to i\to i-1$ and then $i-1\equiv i+1$, impossible for $e\ge3$. The middle $F_iF_tF_i$ path requires $i\to i+1\to i+2$ and then $i+2\equiv i$, also impossible. For $e=2$, $a_{it}=-2$ and every cubic Serre term $E_i^{3-r}E_tE_i^r$ ($0\le r\le3$) has at least one side exponent at least $2$, so it vanishes; the same holds for $F$. These arguments check all derived relations, including the double edge. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.3 The affinized space is well defined and carries the displayed operators. By [F5] each $u_m$ is $z^{a(m)}v_{j(m)}$ for a unique pair, so $\{u_m\}$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$. The formulas $E_iu_m=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}u_{m-1}$ and $F_iu_m=\delta_{m\equiv i}u_{m+1}$ define linear endomorphisms, and they agree with the $z$-picture: if $m=j-ae$ with $j\equiv i+1$ and $j\ne1$, then $m-1=(j-1)-ae$ and $u_{m-1}=z^av_{j-1}$, while for $j=1$ one has $m=1-ae$, $m-1=e-(a+1)e$ and $u_{m-1}=z^{a+1}v_e$, matching $E_i(z^av_1)=z^{a+\delta_{i0}}v_e$ because $j=1\equiv i+1$ forces $i=0$; the $F_i$ computation is the mirror image. [F5, given, algebra]

2.1 $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is a full $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module with the stated weights and integrable strings. If $E_iu_m\ne0$, then $\mathrm{wt}(u_{m-1})-\mathrm{wt}(u_m)=\alpha_i$: for $j(m)\ge2$ this is $\lambda_{j(m)-1}-\lambda_{j(m)}$; for $j(m)=1$ the new pair is $(e,a(m)+1)$, giving $\lambda_e+\delta-\lambda_1=\alpha_0$ by [F3]. Reversing these arrows gives weight difference $-\alpha_i$ for $F_i$. Hence the full toral conjugation relations hold for every $h\in P^\vee$, and the additive weight pairing gives $K_0=1$ and $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$. The mixed and Serre computations of step 1.2 apply to the same integer residue paths on $u_m$; when a same-color mixed composition is nonzero, its two opposite steps return to $u_m$, so their coefficients and the $K_i$ commutator are unchanged. Thus [F1] gives the full module structure, and $K_du_m=q^{a(m)}u_m$ by [F6]. Each color acts on disjoint pairs $\{u_{i+ke},u_{i+ke+1}\}$ with $K_i$ eigenvalues $q,q^{-1}$ and one-step raising and lowering maps, and on singleton vectors of other residues with $K_i$ eigenvalue $1$ and both maps zero. Every basis vector therefore lies in a finite-dimensional rank-one stable space, so the module is integrable and its displayed weight decomposition has level $0$. Finally multiplication by $z$ commutes with $E_i,F_i$ and every derived $K_h$, since $\langle\delta,h\rangle=0$ there. The subspace $(z-1)V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is consequently stable under the genuine subalgebra $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$, and its quotient, identified with $V$ by $z^av_j\mapsto v_j$, carries exactly the finite operators of step 1.2. This proves the claimed derived module action without assigning $K_d$ to finite $V$. [step 1.2, step 1.3, F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, algebra]

3.1 The crystal data of $u_m$ and $b_j$ are as displayed. By step 2.1, $F_iu_m\ne0$ exactly when $m\equiv i$, and then the image is $u_{m+1}$, so the $i$-string through $u_m$ has length $\varphi_i(u_m)=\delta_{m\equiv i}$; dually the $e_i$-string has length $\varepsilon_i(u_m)=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}$. Hence $\varepsilon(u_m)=\sum_i\delta_{m\equiv i+1}\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}}=\Lambda^{\mathrm{cl}}_{j(m)-1}$ and $\varphi(u_m)=\Lambda^{\mathrm{cl}}_{j(m)}$, which lie in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$ and have level $1$ by [F4]; the consistency identity $\varphi_i(u_m)=\varepsilon_i(u_m)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(u_m)\rangle$ holds because $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(u_m)\rangle=\delta_{i,j(m)}-\delta_{i,j(m)-1}$ by [F6]. On $B$ the same computation with $\mathrm{wt}(b_j)=\lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}$ gives $f_ib_j=b_{j+1}$ for $j\equiv i$, $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ for $j\equiv i+1$, $\varepsilon(b_j)=\Lambda_{j-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}$, $\varphi(b_j)=\Lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}$, and the two maps $j\mapsto\Lambda_{j-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $j\mapsto\Lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}$ are bijections from $\{1,\dots,e\}$ onto the $e$ level-one fundamental classes $\{\Lambda_0^{\mathrm{cl}},\dots,\Lambda_{e-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}\}$. [step 2.1, F4, F6, given, algebra]

4.1 The opposite-channel tensor rule is a crystal rule on $B_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{aff}}$. For one fixed color write $+$ for a top vector with $(\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i)=(0,1)$, $-$ for its bottom vector with $(1,0)$, and $o$ for a singleton with $(0,0)$. The displayed rule gives exactly the strings $++\xrightarrow{f_i}+-\xrightarrow{f_i}--$, $+o\xrightarrow{f_i}-o$, and $o+\xrightarrow{f_i}o-$, with $-+$ and $oo$ isolated; the displayed $e_i$ reverses each arrow, including the ties. Thus the string lengths $(\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i)$ are respectively $(0,2),(1,1),(2,0)$ on the first string, $(0,1),(1,0)$ on the next two strings, and $(0,0)$ on the isolated pairs. These nine cases give $\varepsilon_i(x\otimes y)=\max(\varepsilon_i(x)-\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(y)\rangle,\varepsilon_i(y))$ and $\varphi_i(x\otimes y)=\max(\varphi_i(x),\varphi_i(y)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(x)\rangle)$, using step 3.1 on the factors. They imply $\varphi_i-\varepsilon_i=\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(x)+\mathrm{wt}(y)\rangle$; each arrow changes the additive weight by $-\alpha_i$ and its inverse by $\alpha_i$. This verifies the claimed rule, which is the opposite-coproduct $\otimes_+$ rule in the cited KMPY section. [step 2.1, step 3.1, given, algebra]

5.1 The energy function is constant on every connected component of the crystal graph $B_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{aff}}$ for the rule of step 4.1. Write $x=z^ab_j$ with $m=j-ae$ and $y=z^bb_k$ with $n=k-be$, so $H_{\mathrm{op}}(x\otimes y)=\chi(j>k)+b-a$. By step 4.1 the arrow $f_i$ acts on the first factor precisely when $\varepsilon_i(x)\ge\varphi_i(y)$ and on the second factor when $\varepsilon_i(x)<\varphi_i(y)$, and an arrow is nonzero only when the selected factor lies in the domain of $f_i$; explicitly, the first-factor case is nonzero exactly for $j\equiv i$ (whence $\varepsilon_i(x)=0$) and $k\not\equiv i$ (whence $\varphi_i(y)=0$), and the second-factor case is nonzero exactly for $k\equiv i$ and $j\not\equiv i+1$. In the first case the new pair is $(z^{a'}b_{j'},z^bb_k)$ with $j'=j+1,a'=a$ if $j\ne e$, and with $j'=1,a'=a-1$ if $j=e$ (then $i=0$): for $j\ne e$ one has $k\ne j$, so $\chi(j'>k)=\chi(j>k)$, and for $j=e$ one has $k\le e-1$, so $\chi(j'>k)-\chi(j>k)=[1>k]-1=-1$ while $a'-a=-1$, giving $\Delta H=(b-a')-(b-a)+(-1)=1-1=0$. In the second case the new pair is $(z^ab_j,z^{b'}b_{k'})$ with $k'=k+1,b'=b$ if $k\ne e$, and $k'=1,b'=b-1$ if $k=e$ (then $i=0$): for $k\ne e$ one has $j\ne k+1$, so $\chi(j>k')=\chi(j>k)$, and for $k=e$ one has $j\ne1$, so $\chi(j>1)-\chi(j>e)=1-0=1$ while $b'-b=-1$, giving $\Delta H=1-1=0$. The defining rule is reversible by $e_i$, so every edge of the graph is covered by these two cases and $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is constant on components. [step 4.1, given, algebra]

6.1 The energy function has the two loop-shift axioms, vanishes on extremal diagonals and has the stated positivity criterion. For $x=z^ab_j$ and $y=z^bb_k$: $H_{\mathrm{op}}(zx\otimes y)=\chi(j>k)+b-(a+1)=H_{\mathrm{op}}(x\otimes y)-1$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}(x\otimes zy)=\chi(j>k)+(b+1)-a=H_{\mathrm{op}}(x\otimes y)+1$, which are the two axioms (E1) and (E2); $H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^ab_j)=0$ for every $j,a$, which includes every extremal element $z^ab_j$ because every color string through any $b_j$ is a singleton or a one-arrow string: at positive label the raising map vanishes and the Weyl reflection follows the lowering arrow, at negative label the lowering map vanishes and the reflection follows the raising arrow, and at zero label both vanish; these reflections stay in $B$, and the same argument with the loop shifts stays in $B_{\mathrm{aff}}$, so the normalization (E4) holds. For $m_1=j-ae$ and $m_2=k-be$: if $j>k$ then $m_1-m_2=(j-k)+(b-a)e$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}=\chi+ b-a$; the case $b\ge a$ gives $H_{\mathrm{op}}\ge1$ and $m_1-m_2\ge1$; the case $b<a$ gives $H_{\mathrm{op}}\le0$ and $m_1-m_2\le(j-k)-e\le e-1-e<0$. If $j\le k$ then $H_{\mathrm{op}}=b-a$, and $m_1>m_2$ forces $(b-a)e>k-j\ge0$, so $b>a$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}>0$; conversely $b>a$ gives $H_{\mathrm{op}}>0$ and $m_1-m_2=(j-k)+(b-a)e\ge e-(k-j)\ge1$. Hence in all cases $H_{\mathrm{op}}(x\otimes y)>0\iff m_1>m_2$, and this criterion includes $e=2$. [step 3.1, step 5.1, given, algebra]

7.1 The ground sequence satisfies the two ground identities. Let $b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$ and write $M-s=j-ae$ and $M-s-1=k-be$ with $j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$. If $j\ne1$ then $k=j-1$ and $b=a$; if $j=1$ then $k=e$ and $b=a+1$. In the first case $\chi(j>k)=1$ and $b-a=0$, in the second $\chi(1>e)=0$ and $b-a=1$; hence $H_{\mathrm{op}}(b^\circ_s\otimes b^\circ_{s+1})=1$ in both cases, for every $M$ and every $s\ge0$. For the $\varepsilon$-$\varphi$ identity: $b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$ has $\varepsilon(b^\circ_s)=\Lambda^{\mathrm{cl}}_{j-1}$ and $b^\circ_{s+1}=u_{M-s-1}$ has $\varphi(b^\circ_{s+1})=\Lambda^{\mathrm{cl}}_k$, and $k\equiv M-s-1\equiv j-1$ in $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ with $k=j-1$ when $j\ne1$ and $k=e$ representing $0=j-1$ when $j=1$; hence $\varepsilon(b^\circ_s)=\varphi(b^\circ_{s+1})$. [step 3.1, step 6.1, given, algebra]

8.1 Conclusion. The derived module $V$ is a well-defined finite-dimensional $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-module of level $0$ with basis $v_j$ of classical weights $(\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1})^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and crystal operators $f_ib_j=b_{j+1}$ for $j\equiv i$, $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ for $j\equiv i+1$, with $\varepsilon(b_j)=\Lambda^{\mathrm{cl}}_{j-1}$, $\varphi(b_j)=\Lambda^{\mathrm{cl}}_{j}$, both of level $1$, by steps 1.1, 1.2 and 3.1; its affinization $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ has basis $u_m=z^{a}v_j$ with $m=j-ae$, weights $\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}+a\delta$ and $K_d$ eigenvalue $q^a$, carries the integrable action $E_iu_m=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}u_{m-1}$, $F_iu_m=\delta_{m\equiv i}u_{m+1}$ by step 2.1, and has ordinary order $u_m>u_n\iff m>n$; the opposite-channel tensor rule and energy $H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k)=\chi(j>k)+b-a$ with $l(z^ab_j)=ae-j$ satisfy the two loop-shift axioms, constancy on components, the extremal normalization and the positivity criterion by steps 5.1 and 6.1; and the charge-$M$ ground sequence $b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$ satisfies $\varepsilon(b^\circ_s)=\varphi(b^\circ_{s+1})$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}(b^\circ_s\otimes b^\circ_{s+1})=1$ by step 7.1. All statements hold for every $e\ge2$. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1] ∎

## Remarks

- The residue convention is fixed once and for all: $v_j$ represents the residue
  $j\in\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ with $j=e$ representing $0$, and $E_i$ raises the weight by $\alpha_i$ (it lowers $j$ by $1$ when $j\equiv i+1$), while $F_i$ lowers the weight by $\alpha_i$. In the partition model, these correspond respectively to removing and adding a node of residue $i$. This matches the node convention
  $c-r$ of the partition Fock space below.

- The energy function is defined in the channel opposite to the fixed coproduct
  of the library: its tensor rule compares $\varepsilon_i$ of the first factor
  with $\varphi_i$ of the second, and it is $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ and not $H$ that
  the normal-ordering rule uses. Passing between the two channels is the content
  of [[lem-the-q-wedge-relations-coincide-with-the-type-a-energy-braiding-kernel]].

- After the ground state is fixed, every element of the ground sequence is
  determined; an overall loop shift changes the charge and the phase of
  $b^\circ_0$, so the sequence is not determined independently of that choice.

- The finite module $V$ is a level-$0$ $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-module whose crystal
  $\varepsilon,\varphi$ take the level-$1$ values; the level refers to the target
  of $\varepsilon,\varphi$ and not to the weights of $V$. The vector
  representation itself never carries level-$1$ weights.

after.title: Tail estimates: q-adic vanishing against the vacuum and finiteness of the weight strings
after.statement:
Let $F^{(M)}$ be the charge-$M$ Fock space with ground sequence
$b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$ and let $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ be the opposite-channel energy.
Then:

(i) **Vanishing against the right tail.** For a fixed type-A ground sequence,
the condition $H_{\mathrm{op}}(b\otimes b^\circ_s)\le0$ means that the added
integer index lies inside or below the filled right tail
$\{M-s,M-s-1,\dots\}$; then $b\wedge b^\circ_s\wedge b^\circ_{s+1}\wedge\cdots=0$,
a sufficiently long finite prefix of this entire filled-tail wedge is already $0$, and hence the element lies in $q^nW_0$ for
every $n$.

(ii) **Dual left tail.** The mirrored condition with the left tail gives the
same exact finite vanishing, with the roles of left and right exchanged.

(iii) **Endomorphisms commuting with the loop.** A nonzero-weight endomorphism
$C$ of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ commuting with $z$ has only finitely many
loop-shift/color terms on each fundamental vector; inserting $C$ deep inside a
ground tail is eventually $0$, so it converges $q$-adically to $0$ on every
vector.

(iv) **The period operator.** For the explicit period operator
$T$ on $F^{(M)}$ that prepends $e$ vacuum entries and shifts every old index
down by $e$: $T$ preserves each label-weight/size component, and on the
positive-size-$n$ part its $k$-th power is $0$ as soon as $ke>n$.
Consequently $(1-T)^{-1}=1+T+T^2+\cdots$ is a finite geometric sum on every
nonvacuum weight, and each label weight has only finitely many partition
vectors.
after.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The charge-$M$ Fock space, its normal partition basis, the ground sequence, and the energy $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ with the criterion $H_{\mathrm{op}}>0\iff m_1>m_2$.

[F1] Finite normal words have strictly decreasing indices. Straightening preserves cardinality, total index sum and residue multiset, and keeps all indices between the input extremes. Hence an $r$-factor word supported in an interval of fewer than $r$ integers is zero. In an interval of exactly $r$ integers there is only one possible normal $r$-tuple, whose sum is the sum of the entire interval ([[thm-normally-ordered-q-wedges-form-a-basis]], [[def-semi-infinite-q-wedge-fock-space-and-q-adic-topology]]).

[F2] $H_{\mathrm{op}}(u_{m_1}\otimes u_{m_2})>0$ iff $m_1>m_2$. Also $u_m=z^av_j$ when $m=j-ae$; thus $z$ shifts an index by $-e$ ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]], [[lem-the-q-wedge-relations-coincide-with-the-type-a-energy-braiding-kernel]]).

[F3] A charge-$M$ normal word has indices $i_j=M+\lambda_j-j+1$. Its size is the finite excess $\sum_{j=1}^R(i_j-(M-j+1))=|\lambda|$ once $R$ contains its nonvacuum part, and its label weight is $\Omega_M-\sum_{\text{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$. The simple roots are independent in the explicit affine datum ([[def-semi-infinite-q-wedge-fock-space-and-q-adic-topology]], [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** straighten finite filled intervals, using cardinality for an added factor and the changed sum for a replaced factor; use the maximum index and the preserved excess for the period operator.

1.1 Right-tail vanishing. Put $L=M-s$. By [F2], $H_{\mathrm{op}}(u_m\otimes u_L)\le0$ is equivalent to $m\le L$. Choose $B\le m$ and truncate the filled tail at $u_B$. The word $u_m\wedge u_L\wedge u_{L-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_B$ has $L-B+2$ factors, all in the interval $[B,L]$, which contains only $L-B+1$ integers. Every normal term of its finite straightening would have that many distinct indices inside the same interval, which is impossible by [F1]. Thus this finite word is zero, as is every longer prefix. Its semi-infinite image is zero and therefore belongs to $q^nW_0$ for every $n$ at each such finite stage (and to $q^nF_0$ in the Fock space). This argument concerns the whole filled tail; it does not assert that $u_m\wedge u_L$ alone is zero when $m<L$. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

1.2 Finite shifts of $C$. Here nonzero weight means that $C$ is homogeneous of a weight $\gamma\ne0$: it maps a weight space of weight $\nu$ into weight $\nu+\gamma$. Write each $Cv_j$ as a finite sum $\sum_{k,a}c_{j,k,a}z^av_k$. Since $Cz=zC$ and $z$ is invertible, $C(z^tv_j)=\sum_{k,a}c_{j,k,a}z^{t+a}v_k$. Thus each term replaces $u_m$ by $u_{m+d}$, where $d=k-j-ae$ belongs to a fixed finite set obtained from the $e$ fundamental vectors; its coefficient depends only on $m\bmod e$. A term with $d=0$ would be the same vector $u_m$ and have weight shift zero, so its coefficient is zero by homogeneity. Choose $D$ bounding the absolute values of all occurring shifts. [F2, given, algebra]

1.3 Definition and gradings of $T$. On an eventually-ground word define $T$ by prepending $u_M\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-e+1}$ and replacing every old index $i_j$ by $i_j-e$. The simultaneous translation by $-e$ preserves the finite wedge relations: all residue differences and index gaps are unchanged. The new ground tail is again the charge-$M$ tail, so this operation respects local kernels and extending a representative by ground entries, and defines a linear endomorphism of $F^{(M)}$. At position $e+j$, its excess above the ground index is $(i_j-e)-(M-(e+j)+1)=i_j-(M-j+1)$; the prepended entries have excess zero. The old residues are unchanged by translation by $e$, and the new ground entries contribute zero residue-count deviation. Hence total size and label weight are preserved before and after straightening, by [F1] and [F3]. In particular $T$ preserves each label-weight/size component; this does not require a permutation of its partition labels. [F1, F3, given, algebra]

1.4 Finite label weights. If $|\lambda;M\rangle$ has fixed label weight $\mu$, then $\Omega_M-\mu=\sum_i n_i\alpha_i$, where $n_i$ counts the residue-$i$ cells. Independence of the simple roots in [F3] uniquely determines all $n_i$ and hence $|\lambda|=\sum_i n_i$. Only finitely many partitions have this size: each has at most that many positive parts, each bounded by the size. Therefore each label weight contains finitely many partition basis vectors. [F3, given, algebra]

2.1 Dual left-tail vanishing. The mirrored filled tail ending at $u_L$ is $\cdots\wedge u_{L+2}\wedge u_{L+1}\wedge u_L$, with an extra factor $u_m$ on its right and the mirrored condition $H_{\mathrm{op}}(u_L\otimes u_m)\le0$, equivalently $m\ge L$. Truncate its left end at any $B\ge m$. The resulting word $u_B\wedge\cdots\wedge u_L\wedge u_m$ has $B-L+2$ factors inside the $B-L+1$ integers of $[L,B]$, so it is zero by the same finite normal-basis count. Extending that left end preserves zero. This is the reversed-interval version of step 1.1 and proves the dual exact finite vanishing and all its $q$-adic estimates. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Deep replacement. Fix an eventually-ground representative of a Fock vector. At a sufficiently deep slot its index is $m$, and the entire local block $u_{m+D}\wedge u_{m+D-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m-D}$ is ground. In a term of the insertion of $C$ at that slot, replace $u_m$ by $u_{m+d}$, where $0<|d|\le D$. This still has exactly $2D+1$ factors, all in $[m-D,m+D]$. Its total index sum is the ground block's sum plus $d$. By [F1] the only possible normal tuple of that cardinality in this interval is the complete ground tuple, whose sum is different. Every normal coefficient must therefore be zero. The block vanishes before it is wedged with the remaining factors, so the insertion is zero at every sufficiently deep slot; the cutoff is uniform for the finite shifts and, by taking a maximum, for any finite linear combination of representatives. These eventual zeros converge to zero in the separated $q$-adic topology. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.3 Nilpotence on positive size. On $|\lambda;M\rangle$, $T^k$ prepends $ke$ ground entries and shifts all old indices down by $ke$. The largest shifted old index is $M+\lambda_1-ke$, so when $ke>\lambda_1$ all indices of the resulting word are at most $M$. Choose a finite prefix of length $R$ whose remainder is ground and whose last ground entry is below every nonground index. Its ground sum is $S_R=\sum_{j=1}^R(M-j+1)$ and its actual sum is $S_R+|\lambda|$, by step 1.3. Every normal $R$-tuple with maximum at most $M$ satisfies $a_j\le M-j+1$, and therefore has sum at most $S_R$. Straightening preserves sum and the upper bound $M$, so no such normal term exists if $|\lambda|>0$. Thus the finite prefix, and hence $T^k|\lambda;M\rangle$, is zero. Equivalently the only normal charge-$M$ semi-infinite word with maximum at most $M$ is the vacuum, excluded by the preserved positive size. Since $\lambda_1\le|\lambda|=n$, $T^k=0$ on the size-$n>0$ part whenever $ke>n$. [F1, F3, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 Geometric inverse. On a positive-size component choose $K$ with $Ke>n$. The finite operator sum $G=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}T^k$ satisfies $(1-T)G=G(1-T)=1-T^K=1$ by step 2.3. This gives the claimed finite geometric inverse on every nonvacuum label weight and the resulting isomorphism for the tail recurrence; no inverse on the vacuum component is asserted. [step 2.3, algebra]

4.1 Conclusion. Steps 1.1 and 2.1 give the right and dual left filled-tail estimates by exact finite vanishing; step 2.2 gives eventual zero for every deep insertion of a loop-commuting homogeneous nonzero-weight endomorphism; steps 1.3, 2.3 and 3.1 give the size-preserving and label-weight-preserving period operator, its positive-size nilpotence bound and finite inverse; and step 1.4 proves finite label-weight components. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 1.3, step 2.3, step 3.1, step 1.4] ∎

## Remarks

- The estimates are proved here in the library's residue convention
  $c-r\bmod e$ with the ground sequence $b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$; none of the
  two-sided-unbounded evaluation statements of the earlier finite ordered
  tensor theory is imported.
