after.title: The vector representation is a perfect crystal of level one and carries a lower global basis
after.statement:
Keep the conventions of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]].
Then:

(i) The derived level-$0$ module $V$ has **level-one perfect crystal**
$B=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$ in the sense of axioms (P1)-(P3): the weights of $V$ are
the finite Weyl orbit of $\lambda^\circ=\Lambda_1-\Lambda_0$ in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$
with one-dimensional weight spaces, $B\otimes B$ is connected,
$\varepsilon(b)\in P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+$ and $\varphi(b)\in P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+$ have
level one for every $b$, the maps $\varepsilon,\varphi:B\to(P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+)_1$
are bijections onto the level-one dominant weights, and
$B_{\min}:=\{b:\langle c,\varepsilon(b)\rangle=1\}$ equals $B$.

(ii) The basis $G(b_j):=v_j$ is a **lower global basis** of $V$ for the ordinary
semilinear bar involution with coefficient bar $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ and
$\overline{v_j}=v_j$: the local $A_0$-lattice $V_0=\bigoplus_j A_0v_j$ is
bar-stable up to $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, the images $b_j=G(b_j)+qV_0$ are the
crystal elements, $\bar{E_iv}=E_i\bar v$ and $\bar{F_iv}=F_i\bar v$ for all
$v\in V$, all nontrivial rank-one strings have exactly two vertices with $E$- and
$F$-coefficients $1$, and all remaining color strings are frozen singletons, and the divided powers
$E_i^{(m)},F_i^{(m)}$ vanish for $m\ge2$. Here
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ are kept distinct, with the separate positive integral chart $\bigoplus_j\mathbb Z[q]v_j$. The Laurent, zero and infinity charts have balanced intersection $\bigoplus_j\mathbb Z v_j$, so this is the actual integral/bar-compatible lower basis.

(iii) The same statements hold on the affinization with
$G(z^ab_j)=z^av_j$, the loop variable fixed by the bar involution, and the full
$P$-weight $\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}+a\delta$; the finite $V$ is a
$U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-module with $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$-weights and is not a
level-one $P$-graded highest weight module.
after.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The vector module $V$, its affinization $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ with the operators $E_i,F_i,K_h$ and the crystal data $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$ of [[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]], the Bar/global basis framework of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]], and the rank-one string formulas of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]].

[F1] On $B$: $f_ib_j=b_{j+1}$ if $j\equiv i$ and $0$ otherwise; $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ if $j\equiv i+1$ and $0$ otherwise; $\varepsilon_i(b_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}$, $\varphi_i(b_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i}$, $\varepsilon(b_j)=\Lambda^{\mathrm{cl}}_{j-1}$, $\varphi(b_j)=\Lambda^{\mathrm{cl}}_j$, and the weights of $V$ are the $\lambda_j=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}$ with multiplicity one ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]).

[F2] $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ has the rank-one subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ with the standard $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$-relations; on the two-dimensional string space $V_i(m)$ spanned by two consecutive basis vectors the operators $E_i,F_i$ are nonzero in both directions with coefficient $1$ and $E_i^{(2)}=F_i^{(2)}=0$ ([[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]], [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

[F3] A crystal lattice is a weight-graded local $A_0$-lattice stable under the normalized Kashiwara operators with residue basis given by the mod-$q$ images; a perfect crystal of level $l$ satisfies (P1)-(P3) with the level-$l$ dominant weights of $P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+$ ([[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]], [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]).

[F4] $\mathbb Q(q)$ is a field and $q$ is transcendental; the finite Weyl group $W$ of the finite subdiagram acts on $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$ through its type $A_{e-1}$ permutation action, preserving levels.



## Verification

**Proof technique:** read the perfectness data off the explicit arrows, prove the connectedness of $B\otimes B$ by a two-sided raising procedure, and verify the lower-basis axioms by the coefficient-one string matrices.

1.1 Perfectness of $B$ except connectedness. By [F1] every $\varepsilon(b_j)=\Lambda_{j-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $\varphi(b_j)=\Lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}$ has level one, and the two maps are bijections $\{1,\dots,e\}\to\{\Lambda_0^{\mathrm{cl}},\dots,\Lambda_{e-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}\}=(P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+)_1$ because both $j\mapsto\Lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $j\mapsto\Lambda_{j-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ run through the $e$ fundamental classes; hence $B_{\min}=\{b:\langle c,\varepsilon(b)\rangle=1\}=B$ and axiom (P3) holds. For (P1): the weights $\lambda_j$ of $V$ are pairwise distinct with multiplicity one by [F1], and the finite Weyl group of the subdiagram $I\setminus\{0\}$ acts transitively on them: its reflection $s_i$ exchanges $\lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $\lambda_{i+1}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and fixes the others, so adjacent exchanges reach every weight, so they form the finite Weyl orbit of $\lambda^\circ$ with one-dimensional weight spaces, contained in its convex hull. [F1, F3, F4, given, algebra]

1.2 Connectedness of $B\otimes B$ for the fixed coproduct. Use the fixed strict-$f$/non-strict-$e$ tensor rule. For an off-diagonal pair $(b_a,b_b)$ take $i\equiv a-1$. Then $\varphi_i(b_a)=0$ and $\varepsilon_i(b_b)=0$, because $b\ne a$, so the non-strict tie makes $e_i$ act on the first factor and sends $b_a$ to $b_{a-1}$ with cyclic representatives. Repeat until the first factor equals the second; at most $e-1$ steps are needed. From $(b_j,b_j)$, $f_j$ acts first on the first factor since $1>0$, producing $(b_{j+1},b_j)$, then on the second factor since $0\le0$, producing $(b_{j+1},b_{j+1})$. Thus every pair is connected to a diagonal and all diagonals are mutually connected, proving (P2). No attempt to apply $e_b$ to an arbitrary $b_a$ is made. [F1, F3, given, algebra]

1.3 Lower basis and separated charts of $V$. Define coefficient bar by $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ and $\bar v_j=v_j$. The matrices of $E_i,F_i$ have entries $0,1$, so $\overline{E_iv}=E_i\bar v$ and $\overline{F_iv}=F_i\bar v$; derived torals satisfy the corresponding bar-inverted toral identity. Put $V_A=\bigoplus_j A v_j$, $V_0=\bigoplus_j A_0v_j$ and $V_\infty=\bar V_0$. Their intersection is $\bigoplus_j\mathbb Z v_j$: coefficientwise an integral Laurent polynomial regular at both zero and infinity is an integer constant. Its residue map at zero is the basis map $v_j\mapsto v_j+qV_0$, giving the balanced integral lifts $G(b_j)=v_j$. For a fixed color the nontrivial string is $v_i,v_{i+1}$, with $F_iv_i=v_{i+1}$ and $E_iv_{i+1}=v_i$ and coefficients $1$. Every other vector is a singleton killed by both operators. Therefore the normalized Kashiwara operators have the same $0,1$ matrices on this basis and preserve the genuine local chart; their residue arrows are $e_i,f_i$ from [F1]. Also $E_i^2=F_i^2=0$, hence the divided operators of order at least two vanish. The positive integral chart $\bigoplus_j\mathbb Z[q]v_j$ is retained separately and is stable here because the matrices are $0,1$; it is not the local coefficient ring. [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 The affinized chart. Put $L_{\mathrm{aff}}:=\bigoplus_m A_0u_m$ and $G(z^ab_j)=z^av_j=u_{j-ae}$; extend the bar involution by $\overline z=z$. Then $\overline{\cdot}$ is semilinear with coefficient bar $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, fixes every $G(z^ab_j)$, and satisfies $\overline{E_iw}=E_i\overline w$, $\overline{F_iw}=F_i\overline w$ for $w\in V_{\mathrm{aff}}$: the only loop shift occurs for $i=0$, where $E_0(z^av_1)=z^{a+1}v_e$ and $\overline{z^{a+1}v_e}=z^{a+1}v_e=E_0\overline{z^av_1}$, and the remaining cases have coefficients in $\{0,1\}$. The weight of $G(z^ab_j)$ is $\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}+a\delta$, and the string bound of step 1.3 is unchanged because each $i$-orbit is either the same nontrivial two-vertex string shifted by loops or a frozen singleton. The finite module $V$ carries only the $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$-weights $\lambda_j$ and no dominant level-one highest weight vector, so it is a level-$0$ $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-module and not a level-one $P$-graded highest weight module; the $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ and positive $\mathbb Z[q]$ charts are used separately and are not identified. [step 1.3, F1, F3, given, algebra]

3.1 Conclusion. The level-$0$ vector module has the level-one perfect crystal $B=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$ with the explicit $\varepsilon,\varphi$, connected tensor square and $B_{\min}=B$; the basis $G(b_j)=v_j$ is a lower global basis of $V$ whose nontrivial $i$-strings have two vertices with coefficients $1$ and whose remaining color strings are frozen singletons and whose divided operators of order $\ge2$ vanish; and the affinized chart $G(z^ab_j)=z^av_j$ has the same properties with the full $P$-weight. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1] ∎

## Remarks

- The connectedness argument uses only the fixed-coproduct tensor rule and the
  explicit arrows; the opposite channel has the mirrored rule and is not needed
  here.

- The supplier [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]] and
  [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]] are batch-6 items still under
  construction at authoring time; their exact uses are axioms (P1)-(P3) in step
  1.1 and the lattice/residue formalism in steps 2.1 and 3.1. The decision is
  left escalated until the suppliers are completed and the interfaces rechecked.

after.title: The q-antisymmetrizer splits the tensor power and its kernel is the sum of the Hecke kernels
after.statement:
Let $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, $Q=q^2$, and let $M_N=V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ carry the action of
[[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]].
Put $A_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$ and
$C_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}Q^{l(w)}=\prod_{r=1}^N(1+Q+\cdots+Q^{r-1})\ne0$.
Then:

(i) $A_NS_i=S_iA_N=QA_N$ and $A_N^2=C_NA_N$. The operator
$P_N=C_N^{-1}A_N$ is a $k$-linear idempotent commuting with the quantum-group action.

(ii) $\ker A_N=\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\ker(S_i+1)$, a sum of $k$-subspaces, and
$M_N=\ker A_N\oplus\operatorname{im}A_N$. The map $[x]\mapsto A_Nx$ identifies
$M_N/\ker A_N$ with $\operatorname{im}A_N$ as quantum-group modules;
$A_N$ acts there by $C_N$, and every $S_i$ acts there by $Q$.

(iii) On two factors put $x=Y_1$, $y=Y_2$, $R=k[x^{\pm1},y^{\pm1}]$ and
$B=k[x+y,(xy)^{\pm1}]$, the symmetric Laurent subring. The complete partial
q-symmetric kernel on the original Laurent-loop vector space is
$$\ker(S+1)=\bigoplus_j B(v_j\otimes v_j)\ \oplus\!\bigoplus_{j<k}\left(Bh_{jk}+Bh'_{jk}\right),$$
where, writing $a_{jk}=v_j\otimes v_k$ and $b_{jk}=v_k\otimes v_j$,
$$h_{jk}=a_{jk}+q^{-1}b_{jk},\qquad h'_{jk}=x b_{jk}+q^{-1}y a_{jk}.$$
Equivalently, it is the $k$-span of $(S-Q)(u_l\otimes u_m)$ for all integers
$l,m$. This kernel is stable under the quantum-group action and symmetric
Laurent multiplication; arbitrary Laurent multiplication need not preserve it.
Its quotient satisfies the full local straightening relations: repeated entries
vanish, and for $l<m$, writing $m-l=ae+b$ with $a\ge0$ and $0\le b<e$,
$$u_l\wedge u_m=\begin{cases}-u_m\wedge u_l,&b=0,\\-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l,&a=0,\ b>0,\\-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l-u_{l+ae}\wedge u_{m-ae}-q^{-1}u_{m-ae}\wedge u_{l+ae},&a>0,\ b>0.\end{cases}$$
The remaining unordered pair in the third case has strictly smaller gap, so
repetition terminates. At $q=1$, $S_i$ specializes to the negative flip,
$A_N$ to $\sum_w(-1)^{l(w)}w$, and $C_N$ to $N!$; the kernel and quotient
are the ordinary local symmetric relations and exterior power.
after.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The generic field $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, $Q=q^2$, the affine tensor action, and the reduced-word operators $S_w$ and $A_N$ above.

[F1] The operators satisfy $S_i^2=(Q-1)S_i+Q$, the braid relations and distant commutativity; they commute with the quantum-group action ([[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]]).

[F2] On residues, $S(a_{jk})=-q b_{jk}$ and $S(b_{jk})=-q a_{jk}+(Q-1)b_{jk}$ for $j<k$, and $S(v_j\otimes v_j)=-v_j\otimes v_j$. For every Laurent polynomial $f$, $S(fw)=s(f)S(w)+(1-Q)y(f-s(f))/(x-y)\,w$, where $s$ exchanges $x,y$ ([[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]]).

[F3] The index convention is $u_m=z^pv_j$ for $m=j-pe$, with $1\le j\le e$ and $p\in\mathbb Z$; $Y_i$ multiplies the indicated slot by $z$ ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** pair Coxeter lengths, telescope products modulo the local kernels, and compute the complete two-factor kernel over the symmetric Laurent subring before deriving the three straightening cases.

1.1 If $l(ws_i)=l(w)+1$, the reduced-word definition gives $S_wS_i=S_{ws_i}$. If $l(ws_i)=l(w)-1$, put $u=ws_i$, so $S_w=S_uS_i$ and the quadratic relation gives $S_wS_i=Q S_u+(Q-1)S_w$. Thus each paired term satisfies $(S_u+S_{us_i})S_i=Q(S_u+S_{us_i})$ for $l(us_i)=l(u)+1$. Summing the disjoint pairs gives $A_NS_i=QA_N$; left pairing gives $S_iA_N=QA_N$. Hence $A_NS_w=Q^{l(w)}A_N$ and $A_N^2=C_NA_N$. Inserting the largest letter into a permutation in each of its $N$ positions gives $\sum_{w\in S_N}Q^{l(w)}=(1+Q+\cdots+Q^{N-1})\sum_{u\in S_{N-1}}Q^{l(u)}$, proving the product formula by induction. It is nonzero in $k$. [F1, given, algebra]

1.2 For $N=2$, the quadratic identity gives $\operatorname{im}(S-Q)\subseteq\ker(S+1)$, and on that kernel $S-Q=-(1+Q)I$, so equality holds. The original two-factor space is the direct sum of the $R$-blocks $R(v_j\otimes v_j)$ and $Ra_{jk}\oplus Rb_{jk}$ for $j<k$. They are preserved by $S$. Every symmetric $f$ commutes with $S$ by [F2]. The ring $R$ equals $B+Bx$: indeed $y=(x+y)-x$, $x^2=(x+y)x-xy$, $x^{-1}=y/(xy)$ and $y^{-1}=x/(xy)$ reduce every Laurent monomial to this form. The sum is direct, since applying $s$ to $f+gx=0$ with $f,g\in B$ and subtracting gives $g(x-y)=0$, hence $g=f=0$. This also identifies $B$ as the symmetric Laurent subring. Consequently it suffices to compute $S-Q$ on $w,xw$ in each residue block; no localization of the tensor space is taken. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Put $J=\sum_i\ker(S_i+1)$. If $(S_i+1)v=0$, then $(Q+1)A_Nv=A_N(S_i+1)v=0$, so $J\subseteq\ker A_N$. Also $(S_i+1)(S_i-Q)=0$, so $(S_i-Q)v\in J$ for every $v$. For any operator word $T_1\cdots T_d$ with each $T_r$ a simple $S_i$, the exact telescoping identity $T_1\cdots T_d-Q^d I=\sum_{r=1}^d Q^{r-1}(T_r-Q I)T_{r+1}\cdots T_d$ shows that $(S_w-Q^{l(w)}I)v\in J$: each summand has its leftmost factor $S_i-Q$ and hence its image in a local kernel. Thus $(A_N-C_N I)v\in J$. If $A_Nv=0$, this gives $C_Nv\in J$, and $C_N\ne0$ gives $v\in J$. Therefore $\ker A_N=J$. [step 1.1, F1, algebra]

2.2 Write $d_j=v_j\otimes v_j$, $h=h_{jk}$ and $h'=h'_{jk}$. Formula [F2] gives $(S-Q)d_j=-(Q+1)d_j$ and $(S-Q)xd_j=-Q(x+y)d_j$. For $j<k$, it gives $(S-Q)a_{jk}=-Qh$, $(S-Q)b_{jk}=-q h$, $(S-Q)xb_{jk}=-Qh'$, and $(S-Q)xa_{jk}=-Q((x+y)h-q^{-1}h')$. By step 1.2 these images generate the entire kernel over $B$, proving the displayed formula. The alternative $(S-Q)$ basis description follows from the same image equality and [F3]. Quantum-group stability follows from [F1], and symmetric-loop stability from [F2]. In particular the correct base vector is $a_{jk}+q^{-1}b_{jk}$; the vector $a_{jk}-q b_{jk}$ instead has eigenvalue $Q$. [step 1.2, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 Since $A_N^2=C_NA_N$, $P_N=C_N^{-1}A_N$ is idempotent. Every $v$ decomposes as $(v-P_Nv)+P_Nv$, and an element in both its kernel and image is zero. Its kernel and image are those of $A_N$, giving the direct sum. The map $[v]\mapsto A_Nv$ is well defined, injective and onto its image; it commutes with the quantum-group action by [F1]. On that image $A_N$ acts by $C_N$ and every $S_i$ acts by $Q$ by step 1.1. Equivalently, $(S_i-Q)v\in J=\ker A_N$ implies that each $S_i$ induces scalar $Q$ on the quotient. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, algebra]

3.2 Equal indices have $u_l\otimes u_l=(xy)^p d_j\in\ker(S+1)$, for $l=j-pe$. If $l<m$ have equal residue, write $l=j-pe$, $m=j-re$. Their symmetric pair is $(x^py^r+x^ry^p)d_j\in Bd_j$, giving ordinary antisymmetry for $b=0$. For distinct residues write $l=j-pe$, $m=k-re$ and $t=xy$. If $j<k$, then $a=p-r\ge0$ and $b=k-j$; the relation for $a=0$ is $t^r h_{jk}$, and for $a>0$ its four tensor terms are exactly $t^r(x^a+y^a)h_{jk}$. If $j>k$, use $a_{kj}=v_k\otimes v_j$, $b_{kj}=v_j\otimes v_k$; now $a=p-r-1\ge0$ and $b=e+k-j$. The relation for $a=0$ is $t^r h'_{kj}$, and for $a>0$ its four terms are exactly $t^r(x^a+y^a)h'_{kj}$. All these vectors lie in the complete kernel of step 2.2, proving precisely the three displayed cases. Moreover $B$ is spanned over $k$ by $t^r$ and $t^r(x^a+y^a)$ with $r\in\mathbb Z$, $a\ge1$: pair each Laurent monomial with its swap and factor their common smaller power. Thus these relations span the entire kernel described in step 2.2, including its diagonal blocks, and give the full quotient presentation. For $a>0,b>0$, $(l+ae,m-ae)=(m-b,l+b)$ is decreasing and both entries lie strictly between $l,m$; the reverse pair has positive gap $ae-b=(a-1)e+(e-b)<ae+b=m-l$, so repeated application terminates. [step 2.2, F2, F3, algebra]

4.1 At $q=1$, formula [F2] loses its divided-difference correction and sends $f(v_j\otimes v_k)$ to $-s(f)(v_k\otimes v_j)$, so $S_i$ is the negative flip on the entire Laurent-loop tensor space. Accordingly $S_w=(-1)^{l(w)}w$, $A_N$ is the signed antisymmetrizer, $C_N=N!$, and the preceding paired-length and kernel arguments remain valid over $\mathbb Q$ since $N!$ and $2$ are nonzero. The local kernel is now the ordinary symmetric two-factor space, giving the usual exterior quotient. This proves every asserted kernel, splitting and straightening claim on the original tensor space. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.2, step 3.2, F2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

All generic arguments are over $\mathbb Q(q)$. The integral lattice and crystal
charts require their separate coefficient rings; no torsion-freeness over a
Laurent ring or residue of its quotient by $q$ is asserted here.

after.title: The q-wedge relations coincide with the type-A energy braiding kernel
after.statement:
On $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ put $a=Y_1/Y_2$ and let $P$ be the
flip of the two tensor factors including their loop variables. Define the
completed normalized left operator

$$R_{\mathrm{fix}}:=(q^2-a)^{-1}\bigl[(a-1)S+q^2-1\bigr],\qquad \psi_{\mathrm{fix}}:=1-q^2a^{-1},$$

where $S$ is the two-factor Hecke operator of
[[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]]
and $(q^2-a)^{-1}$ is expanded $q$-adically as
$-a^{-1}\sum_{r\ge0}(q^2/a)^r$, so $\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}=1-q^2/a$ has constant term $1$. Then:

(i) $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ swaps the two loop variables, fixes every extremal
pure tensor $u\otimes u$, and commutes with the fixed $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-action;
the cleared identity
$\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}(R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1)=(a^{-1}-1)(S+1)$ holds in the Laurent
domain, and since multiplication by $a^{-1}-1$ is injective on the original
Laurent-loop module one has $\ker(R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1)=\ker(S+1)$ there, before
any localization.

(ii) $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ satisfies the normalized Yang-Baxter equation
$R_{12}R_{23}R_{12}=R_{23}R_{12}R_{23}$ on the three-factor completed module.

(iii) The flipped operator $R_{\mathrm{op}}:=PR_{\mathrm{fix}}P$ with
$\psi_{\mathrm{op}}=1-q^2a$ is the opposite-channel ($\otimes_+$) normalized
braiding of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]:
its $q^0$-leading term is
$z^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}b_1\otimes z^{-H_{\mathrm{op}}}b_2$ with the energy
$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k)=\chi(j>k)+b-a$, and its kernel is
$N_{\mathrm{op}}=P\ker(S+1)$, the $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$- and symmetric-loop orbit of the extremal
diagonal generated by
$C_{j,k}=v_j\otimes z^{-\chi(j>k)}v_k+q\,z^{-\chi(j>k)}v_k\otimes v_j$ $(j\ne k)$
and $C_{j,j}=v_j\otimes v_j$. Flipping back gives the fixed-channel quotient
and the normal-ordering relations of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]].
after.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The two-factor Hecke operator $S$ with $S^2=(Q-1)S+Q$, $Q=q^2$, its loop extension $S(fw)=s(f)S(w)+(1-Q)Y_2\frac{f-s(f)}{Y_1-Y_2}w$, the loop variables $Y_1,Y_2$, the flip $P$, and the energy $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ and tensor rule of the opposite channel.

[F1] The finite residue operator $S_0$ satisfies the three-case formula of the affine Hecke action. Writing $s$ for loop-variable exchange, its Laurent-loop extension is $S=S_0s+(1-Q)Y_2(1-s)/(Y_1-Y_2)$; $S$ commutes with $Y_1Y_2$, but not with $a=Y_1/Y_2$ ([[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]]).

[F2] $S$ commutes with the fixed $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-action on two factors, and the loop variables act invertibly with $Y_ju_m=u_{m-e}$; the Laurent polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[Y_1^{\pm1},Y_2^{\pm1}]$ is a domain, so multiplication by a nonzero element is injective on every free module ([[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]]).

[F3] On residue pairs $(j,k)$ the opposite-channel rule is $f$ on the first factor iff $\varepsilon_i(b_1)\ge\varphi_i(b_2)$, and $H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k)=\chi(j>k)+b-a$ satisfies the two loop-shift axioms and $H_{\mathrm{op}}>0\iff m_1>m_2$ ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]).

[F4] In the finite-type vector crystal, $B\otimes B$ is connected and the extremal elements are the $b_j$ on the diagonal ([[lem-the-level-one-vector-representation-has-a-perfect-crystal-with-lower-global-basis]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** clear the denominator of $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$, read the kernel off the cleared identity, verify Yang-Baxter on the Baxterized numerator, and transport the result through the flip.

1.1 The left fraction and loop swap. From [F1], since $(a-1)Y_2=Y_1-Y_2$, the numerator simplifies as an operator to $(a-1)S+Q-1=[(a-1)S_0+Q-1]s$. Thus $R_{\mathrm{fix}}=R_0(a)s$ with $R_0(a)=((a-1)S_0+Q-1)/(Q-a)$, proving $R_{\mathrm{fix}}f=s(f)R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ for every Laurent loop function $f$. In particular it swaps $Y_1,Y_2$. All denominators are LEFT coefficients; no commutation of $S$ with $a$ is used. The inverse is $-a^{-1}\sum_{r\ge0}(Q/a)^r$, defined in the separated $q$-adic loop-module completion. For an extremal diagonal residue tensor $w$, $S_0w=-w$ and the numerator is $(Q-a)w$, so $R_{\mathrm{fix}}w=w$; common loop shifts give the same conclusion for each $u\otimes u$. By [F2] the original Hecke action and loop functions commute with $U_q'$; ratios have total degree zero, so the same operator intertwines the full affine action. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 The exact original-space kernel. Subtracting the identity with LEFT denominator gives $R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1=(Q-a)^{-1}(a-1)(S+1)$. Multiplication on the left by $\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}=-(Q-a)/a$ gives exactly $(a^{-1}-1)(S+1)$. The formal $q$-adic coefficient $\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}$ is invertible, and multiplication by the nonzero Laurent polynomial $a^{-1}-1$ is injective on the original free Laurent-loop module by [F2]. Hence an ORIGINAL Laurent-loop vector is fixed by $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ exactly when it lies in $\ker(S+1)$. No localization of the original kernel and no finite-dimensional weight-space assumption is needed. [step 1.1, F2, given, algebra]

2.2 Yang--Baxter. Use the FINITE residue operators $S_{0,1},S_{0,2}$ with commuting external variables $x,y$, and put $B_i(x)=(x-1)S_{0,i}+Q-1$. Expand $B_1(x)B_2(xy)B_1(y)$ and $B_2(y)B_1(xy)B_2(x)$. Reduce each square with $S_{0,i}^2=(Q-1)S_{0,i}+Q$ and each three-letter braid with $S_{0,1}S_{0,2}S_{0,1}=S_{0,2}S_{0,1}S_{0,2}$. The coefficients of the remaining Hecke words agree, using $(x-1)(y-1)+(x-1)+(y-1)=xy-1$ for the one-letter terms. The denominator is the common commuting product $(Q-x)(Q-xy)(Q-y)$. In step 1.1 the loop swaps supply precisely $x,y,xy$ on the three factors, so this finite-residue identity proves $R_{12}R_{23}R_{12}=R_{23}R_{12}R_{23}$ in the stated completion. It is not an expansion of full affine $S_i$ against noncommuting loop coefficients. [step 1.1, F1, given, algebra]

3.1 The opposite channel and its leading term. Define $R_{\mathrm{op}}=PR_{\mathrm{fix}}P$ with the full loop-and-factor flip. It intertwines the opposite coproduct because $P$ transports the checked fixed action, and its denominator is $1-Qa$. Evaluate $R_0(a)$ from step 1.1 on the three residue cases. At $q=0$ its pre-loop-swap factor is $a^{-1}$ for $j<k$, and $1$ for $j=k$ or $j>k$. Full flip exchanges both the residue order and $a$ with $a^{-1}$; hence the opposite pre-swap factors are $a,1,1$ for $j>k,j=k,j<k$. On $z^av_j\otimes z^bv_k$ the loop swap adds the exponent difference $b-a$, giving $H_{\mathrm{op}}=\chi(j>k)+b-a$ exactly as in [F3]. The opposite normalization and Yang--Baxter identities follow by the same full flip. [step 1.1, step 2.2, F3, algebra]

4.1 The full kernel generators. Step 2.1 and flip give $\ker(R_{\mathrm{op}}-1)=P\ker(S+1)$. The actual two-factor Laurent-loop kernel is generated over symmetric loop functions by the diagonal tensors and, for $j<k$, $h_{jk}=v_j\otimes v_k+q^{-1}v_k\otimes v_j$ and $h'_{jk}=Y_1v_k\otimes v_j+q^{-1}Y_2v_j\otimes v_k$ ([[lem-the-q-antisymmetrizer-determines-the-finite-q-wedge-kernel]]). Their flips, after multiplication by the units $q$ and $(Y_1Y_2)^{-1}$, are exactly the two order cases of the displayed $C_{j,k}$. Thus the displayed $C$ generate the entire original opposite kernel with symmetric loop shifts. To verify the full quantum orbit explicitly in the fixed channel, write $d_j=v_j\otimes v_j$. For $1\le j<e$, $\Delta F_jd_j=q h_{j,j+1}$ and $(\Delta F_j)^2d_j=(q+q^{-1})d_{j+1}$; hence all diagonals and all constant $h_{jk}$ are reached from $d_1$, extending the second index by the intervening finite lowering operators. Also $\Delta E_0d_1=Y_2(v_1\otimes v_e)+qY_1(v_e\otimes v_1)=q h'_{1e}$. For $j+1<k$, $\Delta F_jh'_{jk}=h'_{j+1,k}$, and for $j<k-1$, $\Delta E_{k-1}h'_{jk}=h'_{j,k-1}$; the partner factor has toral eigenvalue $1$ in both cases. These paths reach every $h'_{jk}$ with $j<k$, including $e=2$ where the first affine step already reaches the only such pair. Since symmetric Laurent multiplication commutes with the derived action, this proves that its symmetric-loop orbit contains the entire kernel basis. Conversely every such orbit element remains in the kernel by intertwining and symmetric-loop stability. Flipping proves the exact opposite quantum/symmetric-loop orbit asserted for the $C$ generators. Common loop shifts and symmetric powers produce every Laurent gap. This is the stated quantum AND symmetric-loop orbit, not arbitrary individual loop multiplication of a kernel vector. Flip back therefore gives precisely the full finite straightening quotient. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

5.1 Conclusion. The checked completed left fraction swaps loops, fixes extremal diagonals, intertwines the fixed action and satisfies normalized Yang--Baxter. Its polynomial-cleared identity has injective Laurent multiplier on original vectors, giving the exact original-space kernel. The opposite flip has the stated energy, denominator and full symmetric-loop/quantum kernel generators, and transports back to the fixed finite-wedge quotient. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

## Remarks

- The formula is a **left**-coefficient fraction: $S$ and $a$ do not commute,
  and no right-fraction interpretation of $(q^2-a)^{-1}$ is asserted.

- The norm of the flip is a loop-and-factor flip only; it does not identify the
  source's positive (descending) wedge chart with the library chart, which is
  proved locally in the finite q-wedge space.

There are finitely many possible multisets/permutations; every secondary pair is more balanced, lowering the sorted dominance profile, and leading swaps reduce inversions. A repeated entry gives0. Thus all branches terminate. Independence: apply the finite antisymmetrizer to any finite family of decreasing tensors; its Laurent coefficients specialize atq1 to independent ordinary antisymmetrizations, so a nonzero finite minor remains nonzero in Q(q). This proves field independence. Integral Laurent straightening then proves W_A is free with precisely that basis, not by nonPID torsionfreeness. For the crystal claim, fix i and the occupied set of a normal integer tuple. The pairs(i+ke,i+ke+1) are disjoint even at e=2. Empty/doubly occupied pairs are frozen; a singly occupied pair is a two-vertex string. Shifting an index by1 either stays ordered or collides and vanishes, so every finite orbit is a product of these free bits. In decreasing-index order the projected coproduct coefficients are exactly the standard tensor of highest-weight1 strings; frozen double pairs contribute net K weight0. Existing finite rank-one tensor rule proves A0 string stability, partial inverses and the residue basis on every such block. This supplies the correct lower chart without importing a source-chart identification through the OP flip.

after.title: Normally ordered q-wedges form a basis for every finite wedge length
after.statement:
For every $N\ge1$ the normally ordered wedges
$\{u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}:m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N\}$ of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]] form a
$\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $W_N$ and an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-basis of the
Laurent lattice $W_A$. The straightening algorithm terminates with a
well-founded profile: the total index sum and the ambient index interval are
preserved, secondary pairs become strictly more balanced in the sorted
dominance profile, and a leading adjacent swap decreases the inversion count;
in particular no bound by the initial inversion count alone is used. The
local $A_0$-chart $L_0:=A_0W_0$, where $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ and $W_0$
is the separate $\mathbb Z[q]$-span of the normal wedges, is a crystal basis: for each color $i$, on the occupied set of a normal tuple
the disjoint pairs $(u_{i+ke},u_{i+ke+1})$ behave as two-vertex highest-weight
$1$ strings, empty and doubly occupied pairs are frozen, and a shift of an
index by one either stays ordered or collides to zero; hence the residues of
the ordered wedges are stable under the normalized string operators and give a
crystal of the integrable affine wedge module. The image of the full
$\mathbb Z[q]$-tensor lattice need not equal $W_0$, and negative powers of $q$
in the straightening are not asserted to be triangular at $q=0$.
after.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite wedge quotient, all normally ordered wedges and the charts $W_A,W_0$ of the Statement.

[F1] The complete three-case straightening follows from the original Laurent divided-difference action and terminates with Laurent coefficients and fixed ambient interval and total sum ([[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]).

[F2] The contract of [[lem-the-q-antisymmetrizer-determines-the-finite-q-wedge-kernel]] gives $A_N^2=C_NA_N$, $C_N\ne0$, $\ker A_N=\sum_i\ker(S_i+1)$ and the quotient identification $W_N\cong\operatorname{im}A_N$. On the quotient $S_i=Q=q^2$.

[F3] The actual residue matrix and divided difference specialize at $q=1$ to $S_i=-P_i$, with $P_i$ the factor flip; the divided-difference term vanishes. Consequently $A_N$ specializes to $\sum_w(-1)^{\ell(w)}P_w$, the signed ordinary antisymmetrizer.

[F4] The vector rules are $E_iu_m=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}u_{m-1}$, $F_iu_m=\delta_{m\equiv i}u_{m+1}$, and $K_iu_m=q^{\delta_{m\equiv i}-\delta_{m\equiv i+1}}u_m$; the fixed coproduct is $\Delta E_i=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$ and $\Delta F_i=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ ([[lem-the-level-one-vector-representation-has-a-perfect-crystal-with-lower-global-basis]]).

[F5] Over the local ring $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$, the tensor product of two divided-basis simple rank-one strings has a basis of divided highest-weight strings whose residues permute the tensor-basis residues; the normalized operators preserve its lattice and induce the crystal tensor rule and partial inverses ([[lem-rank-one-tensor-strings-have-the-crystal-limit-rule]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** the finite dominance and signed specialization proof establishes the field and Laurent bases; the rank-one cube calculation and local-ring tensor-string rule establish the complete localized crystal claim.

1.1 Spanning and termination. For any finite tensor combination choose a finite interval containing its indices. In each word the total sum stays fixed under [F1]. Among the finite set of words in this interval of that sum, order first the sorted decreasing prefix-sum list and then the increasing-pair inversion count. Each secondary balanced pair strictly decreases the former, while a leading adjacent swap decreases the latter and leaves the former fixed. The multiset can change in a secondary branch. Thus every branch terminates, either at zero from repeated adjacent indices or at a strictly decreasing tuple. The relations have coefficients in $A$, proving field spanning and Laurent spanning. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 Field independence. For finitely many distinct normal tuples $I_k$, let $t_{I_k}$ be their raw tensors. Each $A_Nt_{I_k}$ is a finite Laurent-polynomial combination of raw tensors, regular at $q=1$. Select the finite union of all their supports as rows. At $q=1$, [F3] gives signed antisymmetrizations. The strictly decreasing raw row $t_{I_j}$ occurs with coefficient $1$ in column $j$ and coefficient $0$ in the other columns: distinct decreasing tuples have distinct index multisets. Therefore the square minor on these rows specializes to the identity determinant $1$ and is nonzero in $\mathbb Q(q)$. If $\sum_k c_k u_{I_k}=0$, [F2] gives $\sum_k c_k A_Nt_{I_k}=0$, so that nonzero minor forces every $c_k=0$. This proves field independence and, with step 1.1, a field basis for every $N$. [F2, F3, step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 Laurent freeness. Step 1.1 supplies Laurent spanning. Any finite $A$-linear relation is also a field-linear relation and is zero coefficientwise by step 2.1. Thus the map from the direct sum of one copy of $A$ for each normal tuple to $W_A$ is both surjective and injective, proving precisely the claimed Laurent basis. No implication from torsionfreeness over a nonprincipal ring is used. The separate positive span is free over $\mathbb Z[q]$ by the same independence. [step 1.1, step 2.1, given, algebra]

3.2 The exact rank-one cube. Fix a color $i$. The integer pairs $(i+ke,i+ke+1)$ are disjoint for every $e\ge2$. An empty pair is inert; a doubly occupied pair is inert because applying $E_i$ or $F_i$ makes a repeated adjacent index, whose wedge is zero. Its net $K_i$-weight is zero. A singly occupied pair is a copy of the highest-weight-one rank-one module. Changing a free bit shifts an index by one and keeps the word decreasing; the only possible obstruction is an already occupied partner, the frozen double-pair case. Hence each block of fixed pair occupancies is, in decreasing pair order, exactly a tensor product of these free rank-one modules. More explicitly, $F_i$ on a free high bit has coefficient $q^{\sum_{s<t}\epsilon_s}$ and $E_i$ on a free low bit has coefficient $q^{-\sum_{s>t}\epsilon_s}$, where $\epsilon_s=1$ for a high bit and $-1$ for a low bit and the sums are over earlier or later free pairs. Frozen pairs contribute zero. Thus the tensor cube identification is an equality of module actions. [F1, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Local crystal stability on every cube. Apply [F5] inductively to a cube with $r$ free pairs. For $r=0,1$ its divided-string basis is its ordinary basis. If the first $r-1$ factors have been written as a direct sum of simple divided strings with an $A_0$-basis whose residues permute the product basis, tensor each string with the final highest-weight-one factor. The finite calculation of [F5] produces a divided-string basis of each such tensor summand whose residues again permute its product residues. Its transition determinant is a unit of $A_0$, so the lattice remains exactly the $A_0$-span of the cube words, and the normalized operators act on these divided strings, preserve this lattice and permute its residues or send them to zero, with partial inverses. Induction proves these assertions for every finite cube. Step 3.2 identifies this lattice with the corresponding block of $L_0$; the block bases are subsets of the normal basis, and their direct sum covers every tuple. Consequently both normalized operators preserve $L_0$ and give the claimed crystal on its normal residues for every color. [F5, step 3.2, step 2.1, algebra]

5.1 The weight and integrability conditions. A normal wedge is a weight vector, since its raw tensor is one and the kernel is quantum-group stable by [F2]; thus the free local span decomposes by weights. It generates $W_N$ by step 2.1. For fixed color every tuple lies in the finite cube of step 3.2, a tensor product of finite rank-one modules; hence $E_i,F_i$ are locally nilpotent on all finite linear combinations. Together with the operator stability, residue basis and partial inverses of step 4.1, this proves that $L_0$ with the normal residues is a crystal basis of the integrable affine wedge module. [F2, step 2.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, given, algebra]

6.1 Conclusion. The normal wedges give the field and Laurent bases and the finite dominance termination profile; the exact rank-one cube action establishes the crystal basis on the separate local chart $L_0=A_0W_0$. The image of the positive tensor lattice is not identified with $W_0$ or $L_0$, and no triangularity of negative straightening powers at zero has been used. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

## Remarks

The necessary ring correction has a concrete two-bit witness: for $e=3,i=1,N=2$, set $h=u_4\wedge u_1$, $x=u_5\wedge u_1$, $y=u_4\wedge u_2$, $z=u_5\wedge u_2$. Then $F_1h=x+qy$, $F_1^{(2)}h=z$, and $s=x-q^{-1}y$ has $E_1s=F_1s=0$. The unique string decomposition is $x=(1+q^2)^{-1}F_1h+q^2(1+q^2)^{-1}s$, giving $\tilde f_1x=(1+q^2)^{-1}z$. This lies in $L_0$ but not in the polynomial span $W_0$; field independence proves the latter assertion. Thus the literal previous polynomial-lattice claim could not be retained.

manifest_field_changes.after:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The quotient and charts in the Definition, with the stated affine Hecke Laurent action.

[F1] The contract of [[lem-the-q-antisymmetrizer-determines-the-finite-q-wedge-kernel]] gives $\ker A_N=\sum_i\ker(S_i+1)$ and $A_NS_i=QA_N$, where $Q=q^2$; therefore each $S_i$ induces the scalar $Q$ on $W_N$. The kernel is stable under the quantum group action.

[F2] The residue operator and its exact Laurent extension are those of [[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]]: $S(fw)=s(f)S(w)+(1-Q)Y_2(f-s(f))/(Y_1-Y_2)w$.

[F3] Each $u_m=Y^{p}v_j$ with $m=j-pe$, $1\le j\le e$, and $Y$ is invertible; the opposite energy is positive exactly for decreasing indices ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]).



## Verification

**Proof technique:** calculate the actual Laurent two-factor kernel vectors and their symmetric-loop multiples, then use finite dominance followed by inversions for termination.

1.1 Symmetric Laurent multiplication preserves $\ker(S+1)$. If $g=s(g)$, [F2] gives $S(gx)=gS(x)$, since the divided difference of $g$ is zero; this applies also to negative common loop shifts $(Y_1Y_2)^r$. On a diagonal $d_j=v_j\otimes v_j$ one has $S(d_j)=-d_j$. For $j<k$, set $w=v_j\otimes v_k$ and $w'=v_k\otimes v_j$; substitution gives $S(w+q^{-1}w')=-(w+q^{-1}w')$. For $j>k$ the divided differences of $Y_1,Y_2$ give $S(Y_1w)=-qY_2w'$ and $S(Y_2w')=-qY_1w+(Q-1)Y_2w'$, so $Y_1w+q^{-1}Y_2w'$ is a $-1$ eigenvector. These calculations take place in the original Laurent tensor space. Their images vanish in every adjacent pair of slots by [F1]. [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 Diagonal and equal-residue relations. A repeated-index tensor is $(Y_1Y_2)^pd_j$ and hence vanishes. If $l<m$ have the same residue, write $l=j-(r+a)e$, $m=j-re$ with $a>0$. The symmetric multiple $(Y_1Y_2)^r(Y_1^a+Y_2^a)d_j$ is in $\ker(S+1)$ by step 1.1; its image is $u_l\wedge u_m+u_m\wedge u_l$, giving the equal-residue relation. No individual nonsymmetric loop multiplier of a kernel vector has been assumed to preserve the kernel. [step 1.1, F1, F3, algebra]

2.2 Distinct residues without wrapping. Write $l=j-pe$, $m=k-re$ with $j<k$. Then $m-l=(p-r)e+(k-j)=ae+b$, so $p=r+a$ and $b=k-j$. If $a=0$, the symmetric common shift $(Y_1Y_2)^r(w+q^{-1}w')$ gives $u_l\wedge u_m=-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l$. If $a>0$, multiply the same kernel vector by the symmetric Laurent polynomial $(Y_1Y_2)^r(Y_1^a+Y_2^a)$. The four resulting images are, with coefficients $1,q^{-1},1,q^{-1}$, respectively $(l,m)$, $(m-ae,l+ae)$, $(l+ae,m-ae)$, $(m,l)$. Their sum is zero, which is precisely the fourth displayed relation. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 Distinct residues across the representative boundary. If $j>k$, the same expressions have $p-r=a+1$ and $b=e+k-j$. The wrapped base kernel vector of step 1.1 is $h=Y_1w+q^{-1}Y_2w'$. For $a=0$, its common shift $(Y_1Y_2)^rh$ gives the third displayed relation. For $a>0$, its symmetric multiple $(Y_1Y_2)^r(Y_1^a+Y_2^a)h$ has images $(l,m)$, $(m,l)$, $(l+ae,m-ae)$ and $(m-ae,l+ae)$ with coefficients $1,q^{-1},1,q^{-1}$. Thus it gives the same fourth relation in this case also. Together with step 2.1 this exhausts all residue and Laurent-exponent configurations. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

4.1 Pair recursion and whole-word termination. In the mixed case the correction indices are $m-b$ and $l+b$, strictly between $l$ and $m$, with gap $ae-b<ae+b$; the first correction pair is already decreasing, and the reverse pair can be rewritten recursively. For a word of length $N$, fix its original interval $[L,U]$ and total sum $T$. Every branch stays among the finitely many integer tuples in $[L,U]^N$ of sum $T$. Sort a tuple decreasingly and list its first $N-1$ prefix sums. Balancing a pair of extremes strictly decreases this list in lexicographic order: the sums of the largest $r$ coordinates cannot increase, and at least one decreases since the sorted multisets differ. A leading adjacent swap preserves this list and decreases by one the number of pairs of positions whose indices are increasing. Hence the lexicographic pair consisting of prefix-sum list and inversion count strictly decreases along each nonzero branch. Its range is finite, so rewriting terminates. Equal adjacent indices vanish; a terminal nonzero word is strictly decreasing. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, given, algebra]

5.1 Charts and energy. All coefficients in the displayed relations belong to $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Step 4.1 therefore expresses every Laurent tensor-lattice image in the $A$-span of the normal wedges; conversely each normal wedge is such an image. These two lattices equal $W_A$. Its positive chart is the separately defined $\mathbb Z[q]$-span $W_0$, and $q$ is a unit on $W_A$, so $W_A/qW_A=0$. The energy criterion is exactly [F3] and concerns the opposite channel. These computations establish every displayed relation and chart assertion in the Definition, using the kernel contract in [F1]. [step 4.1, F1, F3, given, algebra] ∎

Fix a **charge** $M\in\mathbb Z$ and let $W_N$ be the finite q-wedge spaces of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]. For $r\le s$ define
the connecting map
$\varphi_{r,s}(u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r})
=u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r}\wedge u_{M-r}\wedge u_{M-r-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-s+1}$,
so that new entries are the consecutive ground tail
$u_{M-N},u_{M-N-1},\dots$ appended to a prefix of length $N$. The **charge-$M$
Fock space** is the algebraic direct limit $F^{(M)}:=\varinjlim_{N}W_N$ of the
finite wedge spaces along these maps; equivalently it is the quotient of the
eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Write
$|\lambda;M\rangle$ for the image of the normally ordered semi-infinite word
with entries $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ indexed by the positive parts of the
partition $\lambda$, so that the vacuum $\varnothing$ corresponds to
$u_M\wedge u_{M-1}\wedge u_{M-2}\wedge\cdots$.

The **Laurent, positive and integral charts** of $F^{(M)}$ are

$$F_A:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_0:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A_0\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_{\mathbb Z0}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Z[q]\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}],\ A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}.$$

The **separated q-adic topology** on the full field space is the one induced by
the filtration $q^nF_0$, never by $q^nF_A=F_A$; a finite $A_0$-label component
completes to a $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$-lattice, and the full-field component completes
to $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}F^{(M)}_\mu$ for the label-weight
pieces. Separately, the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart completes to a
$\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$-lattice; this completion is not identified with
$\mathbb Q((q))$ and is not asserted to carry a $\mathbb Q$-vector-space
topology.

**Vacuum weights.** For $M=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$
the vacuum $P$-weight $\Omega_M$ is normalised by $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$ and
$\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$; explicitly, if $M=te+r$ with
$0\le r<e$, then

$$\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-\Bigl(\frac{e\,t(t-1)}{2}+tr\Bigr)\delta.$$

The weight of the partition $\lambda$ is
$\Omega_M-\sum_{\text{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$, its size $|\lambda|$ is a separate
grading, and the $d$-eigenvalue is $\Omega_M(d)$ minus the number of residue-$0$
cells; no periodicity $\Omega_M=\Omega_{M-e}+\delta$ is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The charge $M$, the finite wedge spaces $W_N$, the connecting maps $\varphi_{r,s}$, the direct limit $F^{(M)}$, the three charts, the filtration $q^nF_0$, and the normalisation of $\Omega_M$.

[F1] The normally ordered wedges with strictly decreasing indices are a field basis and a Laurent basis in every $W_N$, and the straightening stays inside the index interval ([[thm-normally-ordered-q-wedges-form-a-basis]]).

[F2] $Y_ju_m=u_{m-e}$ inside the $j$-th slot is the loop operator; the residue of $u_m$ is $m\bmod e$ and $\mathrm{wt}(u_m)=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}+a\delta$ for $m=j-ae$ ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]).

[F3] The loop operator $Y=z$ itself shifts a slot by $-e$, so its $e$-th power shifts it by $-e^2$; simultaneous translations preserve local index differences and hence the finite wedge relations. The levels of the vector-weight differences and $\delta$ are $0$ ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]], [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]).



## Verification

**Proof technique:** show the semi-infinite words stabilise and agree with the partition indexing, then compute the vacuum weights by summing the loop exponents.

1.1 Finite-stage spanning and ordered-tail stabilization. Start with a finite word of length $r$ and choose $S\ge r$ so that the last appended ground index $L=M-S+1$ is below all its original indices. Its image at stage $S$ has $S$ entries, all at least $L$. By [F1], its finite straightening is a finite sum of normal tuples $n_1>\cdots>n_S\ge L$. For each resulting tuple put $\lambda_j=n_j-(M-j+1)$. Then $\lambda_S\ge0$ and $\lambda_j\ge\lambda_{j+1}$, so extending by zeros gives a partition. Every subsequent connecting map appends ground indices $M-S,M-S-1,\ldots$, strictly below the normal tuple's last entry; that image is already normal and is the longer prefix of the same partition word. Thus every direct-limit element is a finite combination of partition words with a stable representative under these ordered-tail extensions. Maps with different finite codomains are not equated. [F1, given, algebra]

1.2 Direct verification of the vacuum weights. Let $M=te+r$ with $t\in\mathbb Z$ and $0\le r<e$, and put $\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-[et(t-1)/2+tr]\delta$. It gives $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$. If $r>0$, subtraction of the formula for $M-1=te+(r-1)$ gives $\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\Lambda_r-\Lambda_{r-1}-t\delta=\lambda_r-t\delta$. Here $u_M=z^{-t}v_r$, so this is exactly $\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$ by [F2]. If $r=0$, use $M-1=(t-1)e+(e-1)$: subtraction gives $\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\Lambda_0-\Lambda_{e-1}+(1-t)\delta=\lambda_e+(1-t)\delta$, and $u_M=z^{1-t}v_e$ has precisely this weight. These integer identities also hold for negative $t$. The base value and this recurrence uniquely determine the weights for all integer charges. The partition label is consequently the stipulated $\Omega_M-\sum_{\mathrm{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$, whose $d$-evaluation is $\Omega_M(d)-m_0$ by the explicit datum; size remains the separate grading. No fractional change of an integer loop exponent or infinite unregularized weight sum is used. [F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 Partition indexing and direct-limit independence. An eventually-ground normal word has $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ with $\lambda_k$ weakly decreasing and eventually zero; hence the $\lambda_k$ are nonnegative and form a partition, and every partition gives such a word. For finitely many distinct partitions choose a common prefix length $N$ containing all their nonzero rows and every position where two words differ. Each partition prefix is normal and has last index $i_N\ge M-N+1$. Its next appended index is $M-N$, strictly smaller, so every later image remains a normal basis word, and the distinct partition images remain distinct. If a finite linear combination vanished in the algebraic direct limit, it would vanish at some common later finite stage: a colimit relation uses finitely many connecting-map relations, which can all be moved to that common stage. Independence of the finite normal basis in [F1] then forces every coefficient to vanish. Together with step 1.1, this proves the partition basis without assuming that arbitrary finite words survive tail attachment. [step 1.1, F1, given, algebra]

3.1 The charts and the topology. Each displayed chart is free on the partition basis over its own ring. Both $F_A$ and $F_0$ contain $F_{\mathbb Z0}$, and $F_A\cap F_0=F_{\mathbb Z0}$ coefficientwise: an integral Laurent polynomial is regular at zero exactly when it has no negative powers. Neither chart is identified with the other. A nonzero vector of the local $A_0$-chart has finitely many nonzero coefficients, each of finite $q$-valuation, so $\bigcap_{n\ge0}q^nF_0=0$. On each finite label component the completion of $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ is $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$, and inverting $q$ gives the field completion $\mathbb Q((q))$; the corresponding full-field component is $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}F^{(M)}_\mu$. Separately the completion of the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart is $\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$. The Laurent lattice has $qF_A=F_A$ and therefore supplies no separated $q$-adic filtration. These statements concern the componentwise completions stipulated in the Definition; no full infinite direct sum is identified with a finite-rank completed lattice. [step 2.1, given, algebra]

4.1 Conclusion. The charge-$M$ Fock space is the algebraic direct limit of the finite wedge spaces along the ground tails, with a basis indexed by all partitions, the three charts $F_A,F_0,F_{\mathbb Z0}$ are distinct free lattices, the separated topology is induced by $q^nF_0$ (never by $q^nF_A$), and the vacuum weights are $\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-(\frac{et(t-1)}2+tr)\delta$ for $M=te+r$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 1.2] ∎

Put $Q:=q^2$ and $c:=Q-1$, and let $Y_j$ denote the operator "multiply the $j$-th
tensor factor by $z$", so that $Y_j$ is invertible with
$Y_ju_m=u_{m-e}$ in the $j$-th slot and different $Y_j$ commute.

**The affine Hecke algebra $\tilde H_N$.** For $N\ge1$, $\tilde H_N$ is the
unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra with generators $S_1,\dots,S_{N-1}$ and invertible
$Y_1^{\pm1},\dots,Y_N^{\pm1}$ subject to

$$S_i^2=(Q-1)S_i+Q,\qquad S_iS_{i+1}S_i=S_{i+1}S_iS_{i+1},\qquad S_iS_j=S_jS_i\quad(|i-j|\ge2),$$

$$Y_iY_j=Y_jY_i,\qquad S_iY_j=Y_jS_i\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad S_iY_iS_i=QY_{i+1}.$$

The element $t_i:=-q^{-1}S_i$ then satisfies $(t_i-q^{-1})(t_i+q)=0$; for a
reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}\in S_N$ put $S_w:=S_{i_1}\cdots S_{i_k}$
and $A_N:=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$ (well defined by the braid relations).

**The two-vector operator and its extension.** On residue tensors
$v_j\otimes v_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$) set

$$S(v_j\otimes v_k)=\begin{cases}-q\,v_k\otimes v_j,&j<k,\\ -\,v_j\otimes v_j,&j=k,\\ -q\,v_k\otimes v_j+(Q-1)v_j\otimes v_k,&j>k.\end{cases}$$

For a Laurent monomial $f=Y_1^pY_2^q$ define, with $s(f):=Y_2^pY_1^q$ the
swap of the two loop variables,

$$S(f\,w):=s(f)\,S(w)+(1-Q)\,Y_2\,\frac{f-s(f)}{Y_1-Y_2}\,w\qquad(w\in V\otimes V),$$

and extend linearly; the quotient $(f-s(f))/(Y_1-Y_2)$ is a Laurent polynomial,
so $S$ is a well-defined linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$.
On $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ the generator $S_i$ acts by this operator on
the tensor factors $i,i+1$ and $Y_j$ acts on the $j$-th factor as above; this
defines the **affine Hecke action**. The whole action commutes with the derived quantum group $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$ (the generators $E_i,F_i$ and $K_h$ with $h$ in the span of the simple coroots). Each $S_i$, and therefore $A_N$, also preserves total loop degree and commutes with the full affine quantum-group action. The individual loops instead satisfy $K_dY_jK_d^{-1}=qY_j$. ## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Laurent tensor space and its vector action from [[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]], the displayed operators $S_i,Y_j$, and the fixed coproduct from [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]].

[F1] The vector basis has $u_m=z^av_j$ with $m=j-ae$, $E_i u_m=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}u_{m-1}$, $F_i u_m=\delta_{m\equiv i}u_{m+1}$, and $K_i v_j=q^{\delta_{i,j}-\delta_{i,j-1}}v_j$. In particular $E_0=zE_0^{\mathrm{fin}}$, $F_0=z^{-1}F_0^{\mathrm{fin}}$, $K_du_m=q^a u_m$, and $\mathrm{wt}(u_{m-e})=\mathrm{wt}(u_m)+\delta$ ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]).

[F2] The coproduct is $\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h$, $\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, $\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$, and is coassociative ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** establish the finite residue identities and the divided-difference identities, combine them for the full Laurent Hecke action, and verify coproduct commutation in an ordered residue window for each color.

1.1 Write $x=Y_1,y=Y_2$, let $s$ swap them, and set $D(f)=y(f-s(f))/(x-y)$. For an integer $l>0$, $(x^l-y^l)/(x-y)=\sum_{r=0}^{l-1}x^{l-1-r}y^r$; for $l<0$ it is $-\sum_{r=1}^{-l}x^{-r}y^{r+l-1}$, obtained by factoring $x^{-l}y^{-l}$ from the positive formula, and for $l=0$ it is zero. Factoring a common Laurent monomial proves that $D$ preserves the Laurent ring. The identity $D(fg)=D(f)g+s(f)D(g)$ follows by subtracting $s(f)s(g)$ from $fg$. With $d=y/(x-y)$, $s(d)=-x/(x-y)$ and $d+s(d)=-1$, expansion of $D=d(1-s)$ gives $D^2=-D$ and $sD+Ds=1-s$. These rational computations are identities on Laurent polynomials because the finite sums show that all the operators preserve that ring. [given, algebra]

1.2 Let $T$ be the displayed residue matrix. For $a=v_j\otimes v_k$, $b=v_k\otimes v_j$, $j<k$, one has $T^2a=Qa-qc b$ and $T^2b=-qc a+(Q+c^2)b$, while $T^2d_j=d_j$ on $d_j=v_j\otimes v_j$. Hence $T^2=cT+Q$. The finite braid is also an exact finite residue identity: abbreviate a triple by its order pattern $ijk$, where $1<2<3$, and let $L=T_1T_2T_1$, $R=T_2T_1T_2$. Applying the three-case matrix gives the following common values: $L(111)=R(111)=-111$; $L(112)=R(112)=-Q211$; $L(121)=R(121)=-Q121+qc211$; $L(211)=R(211)=-Q112+qc121+c211$; $L(122)=R(122)=-Q221$; $L(212)=R(212)=-Q212+qc221$; $L(221)=R(221)=-Q122+qc212+c221$; $L(123)=R(123)=-q^3 321$; $L(132)=R(132)=-q^3 231+Qc321$; $L(213)=R(213)=-q^3 312+Qc321$; $L(231)=R(231)=-q^3 132+Qc(312+231)-qc^2 321$; $L(312)=R(312)=-q^3 213+Qc(312+231)-qc^2 321$; $L(321)=R(321)=-q^3 123+Qc(213+132)-qc^2(312+231)+(c^3+Qc)321$. These thirteen patterns exhaust all triples of residues, including repeated residues for $e=2$, proving the finite braid for every $e$. [given, algebra]

1.3 For a nonzero color $i$, let $A=v_i$ be its top vector and $B=v_{i+1}$ its bottom; $K_i$ has eigenvalues $q,q^{-1}$ there and $1$ on every other residue $O$. On the four pairs $AA,AB,BA,BB$, the coproduct maps are $\Delta(E_i):(0,AA,q^{-1}AA,qAB+BA)$ and $\Delta(F_i):(BA+qAB,BB,q^{-1}BB,0)$ respectively. Applying $T$ before or after them gives respectively $T\Delta(E_i)=\Delta(E_i)T:(0,-AA,-q^{-1}AA,-qAB-BA)$ and $T\Delta(F_i)=\Delta(F_i)T:(-BA-qAB,-BB,-q^{-1}BB,0)$. For spectator pairs, $BO\mapsto AO$, $OB\mapsto OA$ under $E_i$, and $AO\mapsto BO$, $OA\mapsto OB$ under $F_i$, with other pairs killed. Since $A,B$ are consecutive residues, every spectator is below both or above both, so the order comparison and the coefficients in $T$ are unchanged by these maps. This proves residue commutation in every case. $T$ also preserves each total derived toral weight because it only permutes residues. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 On the Laurent tensor space the operator is $S=T s-cD$, with $T$ acting only on residues. It commutes with $s,D$ on coefficients. Thus $S^2=T^2-cT(sD+Ds)+c^2D^2=cT+Q-cT(1-s)-c^2D=cS+Q$ by steps 1.1 and 1.2. This proves the quadratic relation on all loop powers, rather than only on residue tensors. Off-adjacent operators commute because their residue matrices and divided differences involve disjoint positions. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 For $i\ne0$, $\Delta(E_i),\Delta(F_i)$ and the derived torals act by constant residue matrices and commute with scalar Laurent multiplication and the coefficient operators $s,D$. Together with step 1.3 and $S=T s-cD$ this proves their commutation with $S$ on every Laurent tensor. In particular the correct extension of a commutator is $[S,\Delta(X)](fw)=s(f)[S,\Delta(X)]w$, since the divided-difference terms cancel; it is not a formula with $f$ instead of $s(f)$. More generally step 1.1 gives $S(fh)=s(f)S(h)-cD(f)h$ for every Laurent tensor $h$, by applying the Leibniz identity to its residue coefficients. [step 1.1, step 1.3, F1, F2, algebra]

3.1 For three adjacent loop variables $z_1,z_2,z_3$ put $b_{ij}=-c z_j/(z_i-z_j)$, $a=b_{12}$, $b=b_{23}$, and $h=b_{13}$. Then $b_{ij}+b_{ji}=c$ and $\delta_0:=ab-h(a+b-c)=0$, the latter following on multiplying by $(z_1-z_2)(z_2-z_3)(z_1-z_3)$. Write $S_i=(T_i-b_{i,i+1})s_i+b_{i,i+1}$. Expand $S_1S_2S_1-S_2S_1S_2$ with every coefficient on the left, using $s_i b_{jk}=b_{s_i(j),s_i(k)}s_i$. After using $T_i^2=cT_i+Q$ and $T_1T_2T_1=T_2T_1T_2$, the coefficients at $1,s_1,s_2,s_1s_2,s_2s_1,s_1s_2s_1$ are respectively $(a-b)\delta_0$, $(T_1-a)\delta_0$, $-(T_2-b)\delta_0$, $0$, $0$, and $-(T_1-T_2)\delta_0$. For example the coefficient at $1$ is $a^2b+h(Q+a(c-a))-b^2a-h(Q+b(c-b))=(a-b)\delta_0$; the longest coefficient is $(T_1-a)(T_2-h)(T_1-b)-(T_2-b)(T_1-h)(T_2-a)=-(T_1-T_2)\delta_0$. Hence all coefficients vanish. Clearing the three differences gives the identity in the original Laurent tensor space, whose injection into its rational coefficient space is faithful; the operators already preserve the Laurent space by step 1.1. This proves the full braid, with no finite-loop truncation assumption. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The loop multiplication operators are invertible and commute. From step 1.1 and the extension formula, for $l>0$ one has $Sx^l=y^lS-c\sum_{r=1}^l x^{l-r}y^r$; for $l<0$ one has $Sx^l=y^lS+c\sum_{r=1}^{-l}x^{-r}y^{r+l}$, and for $l=0$ there is no correction. These identities hold on every tensor by the divided-difference Leibniz formula. In particular $Sx=yS-cy$ and $Sy=xS+cy$. Therefore $SxS=yS^2-cyS=Qy$ by step 2.1. These are precisely the Bernstein and off-adjacent loop relations in the Definition. Finally $t=-q^{-1}S$ satisfies $(t-q^{-1})(t+q)=q^{-2}(S+1)(S-Q)=0$, and equivalently $t^2=(q^{-1}-q)t+1$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 For the affine color use the ordered Laurent basis $w_1=zv_e=u_0$, $w_2=v_1=u_1$, through $w_e=v_{e-1}=u_{e-1}$. For $1\le j<e$, the extension formula gives $S(x(v_e\otimes v_j))=-q y(v_j\otimes v_e)$ and $S(y(v_j\otimes v_e))=-q x(v_e\otimes v_j)+cy(v_j\otimes v_e)$; also $S(xy(v_e\otimes v_e))=-xy(v_e\otimes v_e)$. On the other pairs the residue formula is unchanged. Thus $S$ on $w_a\otimes w_b$ is exactly the same three-case matrix in the order $w_1<\cdots<w_e$, and its extension remains the formula in step 2.2. On this basis $E_0 w_2=w_1$, $F_0w_1=w_2$, with all other images zero, because $E_0=zE_0^{\mathrm{fin}}$ and $F_0=z^{-1}F_0^{\mathrm{fin}}$. Their toral eigenvalues are $q,q^{-1}$ on $w_1,w_2$ and $1$ on spectators. Consequently precisely the finite commutation calculation of step 1.3 applies to color $0$, followed by the constant-matrix Laurent argument of step 2.2. This proves all affine-color commutators on arbitrary positive and negative loop powers. [step 1.1, step 4.1, step 1.3, step 2.2, F1, F2, algebra]

6.1 On two factors $S$ preserves total residue weight and total loop degree: $s$ swaps loop powers and $D$ has total degree zero, since its numerator is multiplied by $y$ and divided by $x-y$. Hence it commutes with $K_h\otimes K_h$ for every full toral $K_h$, including $K_d$. Each $Y_j$ commutes with $E_i,F_i$ and derived torals by [F1], but increases total loop degree by one, giving $K_dY_jK_d^{-1}=qY_j$. For $N>2$, the iterated coproduct of $E_i$ is the sum of terms $1^{\otimes(r-1)}\otimes E_i\otimes (K_i^{-1})^{\otimes(N-r)}$, and that of $F_i$ is the sum $K_i^{\otimes(r-1)}\otimes F_i\otimes1^{\otimes(N-r)}$. The two terms in the adjacent slots combine into their two-factor coproduct; a term outside those slots has either $K_i^{\pm1}\otimes K_i^{\pm1}$ or $1\otimes1$ there. Steps 2.2 and 5.1 and the toral commutation therefore prove $[S_j,\Delta^{(N)}(X)]=0$ for every full generator $X$. Individual $Y_j$ commute with the derived action for the same slotwise reason. [step 1.1, step 2.2, step 5.1, F1, F2, algebra]

7.1 The quadratic, braid, distant, loop and Bernstein identities prove the displayed affine Hecke action on the entire Laurent tensor space. The finite Hecke operators $S_i$ commute with the full quantum-group action; their products $S_w$ are well defined by reduced words and their sum $A_N$ has the same commutation and total-degree properties. The entire affine Hecke action, including each individual loop, commutes with the derived action, with the degree covariance of step 6.1. This establishes exactly the scope and normalization claimed in the Definition. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 2.2, step 5.1, step 6.1] ∎

## Remarks

The loops have degree one, whereas $S_i$ and $A_N$ have degree zero. The action
uses the fixed coproduct throughout; flipping to the opposite channel is a
separate convention change. At $q=1$, $S_i$ is the negative flip, including its
Laurent coefficients.

Fix $e\ge2$ and let $(I,A,D,P,P^\vee,\alpha_i,h_i,\delta,d,c,q)$ be the cyclic
affine type $A$ Cartan datum of
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]], so $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ and
$q_i=q$ for all $i$. Choose once and for all the representatives
$j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ of the residues of $I$, so that $j=e$ represents the residue
$0$; all indices $j-1$, $j+1$ below are read in this representative range.

**The derived vector module.** Put $P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}:=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z h_i$, and let $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$ denote the subalgebra of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ generated by $E_i,F_i,K_h$ with $h\in P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}$. Let $V:=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{e}\mathbb Q(q)v_j$ and
define $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}$), $E_i$, $F_i$
($i\in I$) on $V$ by

$$K_hv_j:=q^{\langle\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1},h\rangle}v_j,\qquad E_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}\,v_{j-1},\qquad F_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i}\,v_{j+1},$$

where $v_0:=v_e$ and $v_{e+1}:=v_1$ are read cyclically, and $\equiv$ refers to
the residues of $I$. The vector $v_j$ has **classical weight**
$\lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}\in P_{\mathrm{cl}}$, where $\lambda_j:=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}\in P$ is the fixed representative used in the affinization, and **residue** $j\in I$. These operators give the derived $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-action; no degree operator $K_d$ is part of this finite action.

**Affinization.** The **affinization** $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis $\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$, identified
with $V\otimes\mathbb Q[z,z^{-1}]$ by $u_m:=z^av_j$ whenever
$m=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$; this representation of
$m$ is unique. On this space the full affine operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee$), $E_i,F_i$ are

$$K_hu_m:=q^{\langle\lambda_j+a\delta,h\rangle}u_m,\qquad E_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}\,u_{m-1},\qquad F_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i}\,u_{m+1},$$

so that in the $z$-picture
$E_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}z^{a+\delta_{i0}}v_{j-1}$ and
$F_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i}z^{a-\delta_{i0}}v_{j+1}$. We write
$\mathrm{wt}(u_m):=\lambda_j+a\delta\in P$ and $l(u_m):=ae-j=-m$; the
**ordinary order** is $u_m>u_n\iff m>n$.

**Crystal data.** Put $B:=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$, $B_{\mathrm{aff}}:=\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$,
and define partial operators $f_i,e_i$ on $B_{\mathrm{aff}}$ by
$f_iu_m:=u_{m+1}$ if $m\equiv i$ and $f_iu_m:=0$ otherwise, and
$e_iu_m:=u_{m-1}$ if $m\equiv i+1$ and $e_iu_m:=0$ otherwise. Let

$$\varepsilon_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i+1},\qquad \varphi_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i},\qquad \varepsilon(u_m):=\sum_i\varepsilon_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},\qquad \varphi(u_m):=\sum_i\varphi_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},$$

in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$. On the finite set $B$ the same formulas apply through
$b_j\leftrightarrow v_j$, so that $f_ib_j=b_{j+1}$ if $j\equiv i$ and $0$
otherwise, and $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ if $j\equiv i+1$ and $0$ otherwise.

**The opposite channel and its energy.** On $B_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{aff}}$
use the tensor rule $\otimes_+$

$$f_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}f_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)\ge\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes f_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)<\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}\qquad e_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}e_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)>\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes e_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)\le\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}$$

and the **energy function**

$$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k):=\chi(j>k)+b-a,\qquad \chi(j>k):=\begin{cases}1,&j>k,\\0,&j\le k,\end{cases}$$

for $a,b\in\mathbb Z$ and $j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$. For a fixed **charge**
$M\in\mathbb Z$ the **ground sequence** is $b^\circ_s:=u_{M-s}$ ($s\ge0$).
